candidates.title: Robert R. Ruffolo, Jr
candidates.text: Robert R. Ruffolo (born April, 1950, in Yonkers, N.Y.) was president of research and development for Wyeth Pharmaceuticals, and corporate Senior Vice President of Wyeth from 2001 to 2008.

candidates.title: Robert R. Ruffolo, Jr
candidates.text: During his career in the pharmaceutical industry, Ruffolo played a significant role in the discovery and/or development of a number of marketed products, including dobutamine (Dobutrex) for the acute management of congestive heart failure, and eprosartan (Teveten) for hypertension.

candidates.title: Robert R. Ruffolo, Jr
candidates.text: He holds the patent for the discovery of use of carvedilol (Coreg) for the treatment of congestive heart failure, and he led the research team that discovered ropinerole (Requip) for Parkinson's Disease.

candidates.title: Metolazone
candidates.text: Metolazone is a thiazide-like diuretic marketed under the brand names Zytanix from Zydus Cadila, Zaroxolyn, and Mykrox.

candidates.title: Metolazone
candidates.text: It is primarily used to treat congestive heart failure and high blood pressure.

candidates.title: Metolazone
candidates.text: Metolazone indirectly decreases the amount of water reabsorbed into the bloodstream by the kidney, so that blood volume decreases and urine volume increases.

candidates.title: Metolazone
candidates.text: This lowers blood pressure and prevents excess fluid accumulation in heart failure.

candidates.title: Metolazone
candidates.text: Metolazone is sometimes used together with loop diuretics such as furosemide or bumetanide, but these highly effective combinations can lead to dehydration and electrolyte abnormalities.

candidates.title: Beta-3 adrenergic antagonist
candidates.text: A Beta-3 adrenergic antagonist (β-adrenoceptor antagonist) is an adrenergic antagonist which blocks the Beta-3 adrenergic receptors of cells, with either high specificity (an antagonist which is selective for β adrenoceptors) like L-748,328, L-748,337 and SR 59,230A or non-specifically (an antagonist for β and for β or β adrenoceptors) like the non-selective betablocker Carvedilol.

candidates.title: Deoxyepinephrine
candidates.text: Deoxyepinephrine, also known by the common names N-methyldopamine and epinine, is an organic compound and natural product that is structurally related to the important neurotransmitters dopamine and epinephrine.

candidates.title: Deoxyepinephrine
candidates.text: All three of these compounds also belong to the catecholamine family.

candidates.title: Deoxyepinephrine
candidates.text: The pharmacology of epinine largely resembles that of its "parent", dopamine.

candidates.title: Deoxyepinephrine
candidates.text: Epinine has been found in plants, insects and animals.

candidates.title: Deoxyepinephrine
candidates.text: It is also of significance as the active metabolic breakdown product of the prodrug ibopamine, which has been used to treat congestive heart failure.

candidates.title: Terry's nails
candidates.text: Terry's nails is a physical condition in which a person's fingernails or toenails appear white with a characteristic "ground glass" appearance without any lunula.

candidates.title: Terry's nails
candidates.text: The condition is thought to be due to a decrease in vascularity and an increase in connective tissue within the nail bed.

candidates.title: Terry's nails
candidates.text: It frequently occurs in the setting of liver failure, cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, congestive heart failure, hyperthyroidism, or malnutrition.

candidates.title: Terry's nails
candidates.text: Eighty percent of patients with severe liver disease have Terry's nails, but they are also found in patients with kidney failure, in patients with congestive heart failure and are described as a brown arc near the ends of the nails.

candidates.title: Terry's nails
candidates.text: The recognition of characteristic nail patterns, such as Terry’s nails, may be a helpful herald for early diagnosis of systemic diseases.

candidates.title: Carvedilol
candidates.text: Carvedilol, sold under the brand name Coreg among others, is a beta blocker used for treating mild to severe congestive heart failure (CHF), left ventricular dysfunction (LVD) following heart attack in people who are otherwise stable, and for treating high blood pressure.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The history of paleontology in the United States refers to the developments and discoveries regarding fossils found within or by people from the United States of America.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: Local paleontology began informally with Native Americans, who have been familiar with fossils for thousands of years.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: They both told myths about them and applied them to practical purposes.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: African slaves also contributed their knowledge; the first reasonably accurate recorded identification of vertebrate fossils in the new world was made by slaves on a South Carolina plantation who recognized the elephant affinities of mammoth molars uncovered there in 1725.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The first major fossil discovery to attract the attention of formally trained scientists were the Ice Age fossils of Kentucky's Big Bone Lick.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: These fossils were studied by eminent intellectuals like France's George Cuvier and local statesmen and frontiersman like Daniel Boone, Benjamin Franklin, William Henry Harrison, Thomas Jefferson, and George Washington.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: By the end of the 18th century possible dinosaur fossils had already been found.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Big Bone Lick State Park is located at Big Bone in Boone County, Kentucky.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The name of the park comes from the Pleistocene megafauna fossils found there.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Mammoths are believed to have been drawn to this location by a salt lick deposited around sulphur springs.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Other animals including forms of bison, caribou, deer, elk, horse, mastodon, moose, musk ox, peccary, sloth, and possibly tapir also grazed the vegetation and salty earth around the springs that the animals relied on for their diet.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The area near the springs was very soft and marshy causing many animals to become stuck with no way to escape.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: It bills itself as "the birthplace of American paleontology", a term which dates from the 1807 expedition by William Clark undertaken at the direction of President Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In Nicholas Cresswell's journal, dated 1774 to 1777, he records a visit in 1775 to what was then called "Elephant Bone Lick."

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In this account, Cresswell describes finding several bones of "prodigious size", as well as tusk fragments, and teeth—one weighing approximately 10 pounds.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: While he assumed the bones were from ancient elephants, the local native traditions claimed the bones to be those of white buffaloes that had been poisoned by the salty water.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Paleontology in Kentucky refers to paleontological research occurring within or conducted by people from the U.S. state of Kentucky.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Kentucky's abundance of exposed sedimentary rock makes it an ideal source of fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The oldest exposed rocks in Kentucky are of Ordovician age.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The geologic column of Kentucky also contains rocks deposited during the ensuing periods until the end of the Pennsylvanian.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During this span of time the state was first home to a warm shallow sea home to an abundance and variety of brachiopods, cephalopods, crinoids, and trilobites.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During the Devonian, a large reef system formed at what is now the Falls of the Ohio.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Swamps covered Kentucky during the ensuing Carboniferous period.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Then a gap spans from the start of the Permian to the Pleistocene, although the gap is interrupted by minor deposits of Cretaceous and Eocene rocks.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: These deposits mainly preserve plant fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Ice Age Kentucky was home to short-faced bear, bison, elk, lions, mammoths, mastodons, and giant ground sloths.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Local Native Americans interpreted fossils of this age at Big Bone Lick as belonging to ancient monsters killed by benevolent mystical little people.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: This same fossil deposit would attract attention from major American figures like George Washington, Daniel Boone, and, especially, Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Amateur fossil collectors should be aware that they need permission from landowners to prospect legally on private property.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Brachiopods are the Kentucky state fossil.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: A significant number of Indonesian men and women who migrate overseas each year to work in the construction, agriculture, manufacturing, and domestic service sectors are subjected to conditions of forced labor or debt bondage in Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Singapore, Taiwan, Hong Kong, United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Syria, France, Belgium, Germany, and the Netherlands.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: Malaysia and Saudi Arabia are the top destinations for legal and illegal Indonesian migrant workers who are trafficked for domestic servitude, commercial sexual exploitation, and forced labor.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: Some labor recruitment companies, known as PJTKIs, operated similarly to trafficking rings, luring both male and female workers into debt bondage, involuntary servitude, and other trafficking situations.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: Some workers, often women intending to migrate, entered trafficking and trafficking-like situations during their attempt to find work abroad through licensed and unlicensed PJTKIs.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: These labor recruiters charged workers high commission fees—up to $3,000—which are not regulated under Indonesian law and often require workers to incur debt to pay, leaving them vulnerable in some instances to situations of debt bondage.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: PJTKIs also reportedly withheld the documents of some workers, and confined them in holding centers, sometimes for periods of many months.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: Some PJTKIs also used threats of violence to maintain control over prospective migrant workers.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: Recruitment agencies routinely falsified birth dates, including for children, in order to apply for passports and migrant worker documents.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia
candidates.text: Women and girls are trafficked into commercial sexual exploitation in Malaysia, Singapore, and throughout Indonesia.

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia

candidates.title: Human trafficking in Indonesia

candidates.text: He was a finalist in the Archibald Prize twenty-four times, including "Nornie Gude (Artist)" (1944) and "Anne and Drew Pendlebury (actress and musician respectively)" (1979).

candidates.title: L. Scott Pendlebury
candidates.text: His work was presented in the state galleries of New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania and Victoria.

candidates.title: L. Scott Pendlebury
candidates.text: Pendlebury worked at Swinburne Technical College as an instructor from 1946 to 1963 and then as head of the art school until his retirement in 1974.

candidates.title: L. Scott Pendlebury
candidates.text: He died in May 1986, aged 72.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Cuthy Mede is a Malawian artist.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Lonely Planet said "possibly the best-known [Malawian] artist is Cuthy Mede – he is also actively involved in the development and promotion of Malawian art within the country and around the world."

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Cuthy Mede grew up on Likoma Island, Lake Malawi where he drew in the rough sands of the beach as a child.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Later he studied Fine Art in Chancellor College and became a lecturer at the College in the 1970s.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: By the 1980s Mede established Gallerie Africaine in Lilongwe City Centre, the first art gallery by a local artist in Malawi.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Mede exhibited his work widely in Malawi, becoming a successful artist selling his work to international collectors.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Mede encouraged the work of young Malawian artists struggling to make a living selling folk art and wood carvings as street traders.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: He also brought fine art work from other Malawian artists into his Gallery.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: He was commissioned to paint a large mural decorating the City Centre.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Mede is best known for his modern art styles: modern, futurist, cubist and pointillist, with strong local themes.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: His paintings depicted local people, historic events and current events in Malawi, Biblical references with local interpretations, indigenous religious expressions, and paintings about ideas such as Justice, Greed, Man and Machine.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: His paintings depict famine, refugees from Mozambique during the Civil War, voting and democracy, wedding celebration, spirits and possession, and the Nyau masquerade.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Mede's less known work is realistic, including a reproduction of the Mona Lisa.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: His best known work is dominated by bright primary colors, cubist style, though his pointillist work favors ochres and softer tones in the overall effect.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: In later years Mede painted mostly in shades of blue, then white on white, the purest light.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Mede is an evangelical Christian and his work begins with a point of light from which the rest of the painting flows, the energy from God.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: This point of light is evident in most of his paintings as a single dot, a sun or moon, or an orb.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Best known for his paintings, Mede also produced sculptural forms such as wood figures covered in beads and pigments.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: His garden in Lilongwe was made into a work of art, in white and light, with fluorescent light tubes hanging from trees and white painted rocks lining the drive and entry.

candidates.title: Cuthy Mede
candidates.text: Mede's wife, Esther (deceased 2009), served as Principal Secretary for the Ministry of Research and Environmental Affairs in the Malawi government.

candidates.title: Also Sprach Zarathustra (painting)
candidates.text: Also sprach Zarathustra (Thus Spoke Zarathustra or Thus Spake Zarathustra) is the oil painting cycle by Lena Hades painted from 1995 to 1997 and inspired by Friedrich Nietzsche's philosophical novel of the same name.

candidates.title: Also Sprach Zarathustra (painting)
candidates.text: The painter created her first painting on December 1995 in Moscow.

candidates.title: Also Sprach Zarathustra (painting)
candidates.text: The "Thus Spake Zarathustra" cycle is a series of twenty-eight oil paintings made by the artist from 1995 to 1997 and thirty graphic works made in 2009.

candidates.title: Also Sprach Zarathustra (painting)
candidates.text: Twenty-four of the paintings depict so-called round-headed little men and their struggles in life.

candidates.title: Also Sprach Zarathustra (painting)
candidates.text: The remaining four depict Zarathustra himself, his eagle and serpent.

candidates.title: Also Sprach Zarathustra (painting)
candidates.text: Six paintings of the series were purchased by the Moscow Museum of Modern Art and by some important private collectors.

candidates.title: Also Sprach Zarathustra (painting)
candidates.text: The oil painting "Also Sprach Zarathustra" series was exhibited several times — including the exhibition at the Institute of Philosophy of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1997 and at the First Moscow Biennale of contemporary art in 2005.

candidates.title: Leonardo Corbucci
candidates.text: Leonardo Corbucci is an award-winning film director from Italy who is now located in Los Angeles US and member of the DGA (Directors Guild of America).

candidates.text: He has won many prizes from the prestigious "Rising Star" at the Canadian International Film Festival to the "Silver Ace" at the Las Vegas International Film festival, "Best Romance" at the Best of Best Film Fest, "Best Experimental Film" at the Idie Gathering, "Best Drama" at the International Family Film Festival, "Best screenplay" at the Sunset Film Festival, "Honorable Mention" at the Queen World Film Festival, "Titoli Price" at the Murgia Film Festival, "Best Short film" at the Burbank Film Festival.

candidates.title: Leonardo Corbucci
candidates.text: His films have been official selections at the Venice Film Festival, Beverly Hills Film Festival, Santa Barbara Film Festival, San Diego IndieFest, Phoenix Film Festival, Riverside Film Festival, Seattle True Independent Film Festival, Ventura Film Festival, Rome Film Festival, Riverband Film Festival and screened at that Cannes Film Festival.

candidates.title: Michael Flessas
candidates.text: Michael C. Flessas (born June 2, 1959 in Miami, Florida), is the birth name of American actor Michael Flessas, who is of Greek ancestry.

candidates.title: Michael Flessas
candidates.text: Flessas' most notable film role was "Angry Man" in the Cannes Film Festival 2000 Palme d'Or winning film "Dancer in the Dark" directed by Danish film director Lars von Trier.

candidates.title: Michael Flessas
candidates.text: Originally, the director himself considered playing the role but, instead, the role was given to Flessas.

candidates.title: Michael Flessas
candidates.text: "Dancer in the Dark" starred Icelandic singer/actress Björk who won the Best Actress award at Cannes for her role.

candidates.title: Michael Flessas
candidates.text: French film icon, César Award winner, and Academy Award nominee Catherine Deneuve, and other noteworthy artists such as Academy Award and Tony Award winner Joel Grey, Peter Stormare, David Morse, and Stellan Skarsgård also performed in the multiple prize winning film.

candidates.title: Michael Flessas
candidates.text: One of Björk's songs for the film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Song.

candidates.title: 2010 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: The 63rd Cannes Film Festival was held from 12 to 23 May 2010, in Cannes, France.

candidates.title: 2010 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: The Cannes Film Festival, hailed as being one of the most recognized and prestigious film festivals worldwide, was founded in 1946.

candidates.title: 2010 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: It consists of having films screened in and out of competition during the festival; films screened in competition compete for the Palme d'Or award.

candidates.title: 2010 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: The award in 2010 was won by "Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives", a Thai film directed by Apichatpong Weerasethakul.

candidates.title: 2010 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: This was determined by the festival's jury members who reviewed films screened in competition.

candidates.title: 2010 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: American film director Tim Burton was the president of the jury for the international competition, and other members of the jury for that competition included actors, screenwriters and composers, such as Kate Beckinsale, Emmanuel Carrère, Benicio del Toro, and Alexandre Desplat.

candidates.title: 2010 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: Other categories for films screened in competition that have their own separate juries for other awards are for Short Films and the Un Certain Regard category.

candidates.title: Arsi Nami
candidates.text: Arsalan Nami (Persian: ارسلان نامی‎ ‎ ) (born May 21, 1984 in Shiraz) better known as Arsi Nami, is a Persian-Swedish singer, songwriter, music therapist, actor and philanthropist living in Los Angeles, California.

candidates.title: Arsi Nami
candidates.text: Credits include music on Fox TV shows Bones (TV series) and The Goodwin Games as well Cannes Film Festival winning film Love is Blind and Crown Prince of Heaven.

candidates.title: Arsi Nami
candidates.text: He was the lead actor and composer in drama shortfilm, Love Is Blind, which won the 2017 Jury Prize at Cannes International Film Festival Entr'2 Marches for sharing disability awareness.

candidates.title: Arsi Nami
candidates.text: His commercial acting credits include giant brands such as Hewlett Packard, Ford Motor Company, Samsung, Disney, NBA, Guitar Center, Los Defensores.

candidates.title: Arsi Nami
candidates.text: Arsi Nami nominated for Best lead male actor in comedy film Villa, a 2017 Official Selection at Premio Tortoreto alla Cultura in Italy, AM Film Festival in Egypt and International Festival of Short Films on Culture & Tourism, India.

candidates.title: Arsi Nami
candidates.text: also one of the lead actors in 2017 European Cinematography Award winning Drama film Camelia as Vincent the painter.

candidates.title: Abderrahmane Sissako
candidates.text: Abderrahmane Sissako (born 13 October 1961) is a Mauritanian film director and producer.

candidates.title: Abderrahmane Sissako
candidates.text: Sissako is, along with Ousmane Sembène, Souleymane Cissé, Idrissa Ouedraogo and Djibril Diop Mambety, one of the few filmmakers from Africa to reach a measure of international influence.

candidates.title: Abderrahmane Sissako
candidates.text: His film "Waiting for Happiness" ("Heremakono") was screened at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival official selection under Un Certain Regard, winning the FIPRESCI Prize.

candidates.title: Abderrahmane Sissako
candidates.text: His 2007 film "Bamako" received much attention.

candidates.title: Abderrahmane Sissako
candidates.text: Sissako's themes include globalisation, exile and the displacement of people.

candidates.title: Abderrahmane Sissako
candidates.text: His 2014 film "Timbuktu" was selected to compete for the Palme d'Or in the main competition section at the 2014 Cannes Film Festival and nominated for an Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

candidates.title: The Silent World
candidates.text: The Silent World (French: Le Monde du silence ) is a 1956 French documentary film co-directed by the famed French oceanographer Jacques-Yves Cousteau and a young Louis Malle.

candidates.title: The Silent World
candidates.text: "The Silent World" is noted as one of the first films to use underwater cinematography to show the ocean depths in color.

candidates.title: The Silent World
candidates.text: Its title derives from Cousteau's 1953 book "".

candidates.title: The Silent World
candidates.text: It was released in the United States by Columbia Pictures.

candidates.title: Zeitgeist (film series)
candidates.text: Zeitgeist is a series of three documentary films released between 2007 and 2011 that present a number of conspiracy theories, as well as proposals for broad social and economic changes.

candidates.title: 1956 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: The 9th Cannes Film Festival was held from 23 April to 10 May 1956.

candidates.title: 1956 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: The Palme d'Or went to "The Silent World" by Jacques-Yves Cousteau and Louis Malle.

candidates.title: 1956 Cannes Film Festival
candidates.text: The festival opened with "Marie-Antoinette reine de France", directed by Jean Delannoy and closed with "Il tetto" by Vittorio De Sica.

candidates.title: And the Pursuit of Happiness
candidates.text: And the Pursuit of Happiness (French: "La poursuite du bonheur" ) is a 1986 documentary film directed by Louis Malle about the experiences of immigrants in the United States during the 1980s.

candidates.title: And the Pursuit of Happiness
candidates.text: It was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 1987 Cannes Film Festival.

candidates.title: Dan Sullivan (EastEnders)
candidates.text: Dan Sullivan is a fictional character from the BBC soap opera "EastEnders", played by Craig Fairbrass.

candidates.title: Dan Sullivan (EastEnders)
candidates.text: Dan appeared on the show as a regular from 7 June 1999 to 10 July 2000 and then as a recurring character from 26 February to 16 August 2001.

candidates.title: Dan Sullivan (EastEnders)
candidates.text: He became central to a plot involving a love triangle between himself, his lover Carol Jackson and Carol's daughter Bianca - whom Dan embarks on an affair with.

candidates.title: Dan Sullivan (EastEnders)
candidates.text: Other major storylines included him being conned out of his share of The Queen Victoria, being framed and wrongly imprisoned for the shooting of archenemy Phil Mitchell and being responsible for the kidnapping of Melanie Owen.

candidates.title: Tamzin Outhwaite
candidates.text: Tamzin Maria Outhwaite ( ; born 5 November 1970) is a British actress from London.

candidates.title: Tamzin Outhwaite
candidates.text: Since coming to national notice playing Melanie Owen in the BBC One soap opera "EastEnders" from 1998 until 2002, she has since starred in both theatre and television productions, including army series "Red Cap" and crime drama "New Tricks".

candidates.title: Joanna Christie
candidates.text: Joanna Lauren Christie (born 10 April 1982) is an English actress and singer.

candidates.title: Joanna Christie
candidates.text: She is noted for her work in the play "Equus" (2007) alongside Daniel Radcliffe, but is best known for her role as Girl in the Broadway musical "Once".

candidates.title: Joanna Christie
candidates.text: Christie played Connie Murphy, one of the lead female characters, in the hit Netflix television series "Narcos".

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: Richard Francis "Ricky" Butcher is a fictional character from the BBC soap opera "EastEnders", played by Sid Owen.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: Introduced as a school boy in 1988, Ricky is one of the longest-running, male protagonists to feature in "EastEnders".

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: Owen originally left the role in 2000 to pursue a music career.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: However, he reprised the role in 2002 before being axed by producer Louise Berridge in 2004.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: In 2008, producer Diederick Santer reintroduced the character for a third time, along with his wife Bianca Jackson (Patsy Palmer).

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: Ricky is portrayed as unintelligent, simplistic, easily led and bossed around by dominant personalities.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: On 26 February 2011, it was announced that Owen would take a temporary break from the show.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: The character exited on 19 July 2011, returning five months later on 13 December 2011.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: Ricky left "EastEnders" on 17 January 2012.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: Ricky returned to "EastEnders" on 20 June 2012 for the wedding of his sister, Janine (Charlie Brooks), before departing for the final time on 29 June 2012.

candidates.title: Ricky Butcher
candidates.text: In April 2016 he had voiced his interest on returning to "EastEnders" during an appearance on "Celebrity Juice".

candidates.title: Harraton
candidates.text: Harraton was a township in Chester-le-Street parish, and a sub-district in Chester-le-Street registration district, Durham.

candidates.title: Harraton
candidates.text: Since 1974 it is located in the City of Sunderland in the county of Tyne and Wear.

candidates.title: Harraton
candidates.text: The township lies on the river Wear, and on the North-eastern railway; now a cyclist route/footpath, 3 miles north-east of Chester-le-Street; includes the villages of Chaters-Hough, Fatfield, and Pictree; and forms part of the chapelry of Birtley.

candidates.title: Harraton
candidates.text: The soil and subsoil are clay.

candidates.title: Harraton
candidates.text: The chief crops are wheat, oats and turnips.

candidates.title: Harraton
candidates.text: A considerable portion of Lambton Park, the seat of the Earl of Durham, and the castle and gardens, being on the north side of the river Wear, are in the township of Harraton, but for particulars see Lambton Castle.

candidates.title: Empty Orchestra
candidates.text: "Empty Orchestra" is the fourth episode of the third series of the British dark comedy anthology television programme "Inside No. 9".

candidates.title: Empty Orchestra
candidates.text: Written by Steve Pemberton and Reece Shearsmith and directed by Guillem Morales, the episode first aired on 7 March 2017, on BBC 2.

candidates.title: Empty Orchestra
candidates.text: The episode is set in a karaoke booth, and follows a group of work colleagues—Greg (Shearsmith), Fran (Sarah Hadland), Connie (Tamzin Outhwaite), Janet (Emily Howlett) and Duane (Javone Prince)—celebrating the promotion of Roger (Pemberton).

candidates.title: Empty Orchestra
candidates.text: Rebekah Hinds also stars.

candidates.title: Paradox (TV series)
candidates.text: Written by Lizzie Mickery and produced by Clerkenwell Films for the BBC, it was filmed and set in Manchester, England.

candidates.title: KRWB (AM)

candidates.text: They share studios at 113 Lake St NW, in Warroad.

candidates.title: Angle Inlet, Minnesota
candidates.text: Angle Inlet is a census-designated place (CDP) and unincorporated community in Angle Township, Lake of the Woods County, Minnesota, United States.

candidates.title: Angle Inlet, Minnesota
candidates.text: Its population was 60 as of the 2010 census.

candidates.title: Angle Inlet, Minnesota
candidates.text: The community is part of the Northwest Angle, the only place in the contiguous United States north of the 49th parallel; it is the northernmost census-designated place in the contiguous United States.

candidates.title: Angle Inlet, Minnesota
candidates.text: The French built Fort Saint Charles nearby in 1732.

candidates.title: Penasse, Minnesota
candidates.text: Penasse is an unincorporated community in Angle Township, Lake of the Woods County, Minnesota, United States.

candidates.title: Penasse, Minnesota
candidates.text: Penasse is located on Penasse Island in Lake of the Woods, in the northern part of Northwest Angle.

candidates.title: Penasse, Minnesota
candidates.text: Its location makes it the northernmost populated place in the contiguous United States.

candidates.title: Penasse, Minnesota
candidates.text: The community was named for Tom Penasse, an American Indian from the area; it had a post office from 1920 to 1969.

candidates.title: Penasse, Minnesota
candidates.text: The French built Fort Saint Charles nearby in 1732.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: KLIK (1240 AM), branding as Newstalk 1240, is a radio station broadcasting a News Talk Information format.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: Licensed to Jefferson City, Missouri, United States, the station serves the Columbia, Missouri area.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: The station is currently owned by Cumulus Media and features programing from ABC Radio and Westwood One.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: KLIK also operates a local news operation with sister station KFRU (1400 AM in Columbia, Missouri).

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: From 1954 until September 8, 1999, KLIK was located at 950 AM, transmitting with a daytime power of 5000 watts and a nighttime power of 500 watts (directional) from a four tower array about 3.2 miles south of Jefferson City.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: Early owners of KLIK broadcast a varied format of news and talk programs including music programs of middle of the road, top 40, adult contemporary and country music as 95 KLIK.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: For many years, KLIK and KJFF as the two largest regional radio stations (the most powerful AM and FM station in the region) dominated radio listenership in cumulative market share in the Columbia-Jeff City Market of Central Missouri.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: In the 1970s and early 1980s KLIK was known as the Live 95 as its broadcasts were all programmed by live deejays, talk hosts and newscasters rather than by a satellite or automation system.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: KLIK once operated with an FM sister station in the 1970s and 1980s known was KJFF 106.9 FM a 100,000 watt semi-automated easy listening music station with a large regional coverage signal.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: In the early 1980s KLIK and KJFF-FM together were sold by the local Jefferson City operators to a regional group broadcaster, and newspaper publisher, Brill Media.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: In about 1982, KJFF-FM 106.9 FM became an adult contemporary music station, initially with a satellite delivered music format, and easy listening music was phased out along with the KJFF call letters which were replaced by the new FM call signs of KTXY.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: KLIK 950 AM transitioned over from AC/Contemporary music at about the same time to a 24-hour-a-day live country/western format known as 95 Country.

candidates.title: KLIK
candidates.text: KLIK carried a variety of programming and a mostly country music format until the late 1990s.

candidates.title: Northwest Angle
candidates.text: The Northwest Angle, known simply as the Angle by locals, and coextensive with Angle Township, is a part of northern Lake of the Woods County, Minnesota.

candidates.title: Northwest Angle
candidates.text: Except for minor surveying errors, it is the only place in the United States outside Alaska that is north of the 49th parallel, which forms the border between the U.S. and Canada from the Northwest Angle westward to the Strait of Georgia (between the state of Washington and the province of British Columbia).

candidates.title: Northwest Angle
candidates.text: The land area of the Angle is separated from the rest of Minnesota by Lake of the Woods, but shares a land border with Canada.

candidates.title: Northwest Angle
candidates.text: It is one of only six non-island locations in the 48 contiguous states that are practical exclaves of the U.S.

candidates.title: Northwest Angle
candidates.text: It is the northernmost township in Minnesota and contains the northernmost point in the contiguous 48 states.

candidates.title: Northwest Angle
candidates.text: The unincorporated community of Angle Inlet is located in the Northwest Angle.

candidates.title: Fort Saint Charles
candidates.text: Fort Saint Charles (1732) on Lake of the Woods was the second post built by La Vérendrye during his expansion of trade and exploration west of Lake Superior.

candidates.title: Fort Saint Charles
candidates.text: It was located on Magnusens Island on the Northwest Angle of Minnesota, 3.5 miles east of Angle Inlet, Minnesota and one mile southwest of Penasse, Minnesota, the most northerly point in that state.

candidates.title: Fort Saint Charles
candidates.text: The site of the modern reconstruction may be somewhat different since the lake levels were raised by control structures on the Winnipeg River.

candidates.title: Fort Saint Charles
candidates.text: For related forts see Winnipeg River.

candidates.title: Ritu Nanda
candidates.text: Ritu Nanda (born Ritu Kapoor; 30 October 1948) is a prominent insurance advisor associated chiefly with the life insurance business.

candidates.title: Ritu Nanda
candidates.text: She is currently the chairman and chief executive officer of Ritu Nanda Insurance Services (RNIS).

candidates.title: Ritu Nanda
candidates.text: Nanda was initially managing a household appliances manufacturing business Nikitasha which got closed due to poor growth.

candidates.title: Ritu Nanda
candidates.text: On recommendation of her friend, she decided to be an insurance agent.

candidates.title: Escorts Group
candidates.text: The Escorts Group is an Indian engineering company that operates in the sectors of agri-machinery, construction and material handling equipment, railway equipment and auto components.

candidates.title: Escorts Group
candidates.text: Headquartered in Faridabad, Haryana, the company was launched in 1944 and has marketing operations in more than 40 countries.

candidates.title: Escorts Group
candidates.text: Escorts Group’s management team includes Rajan Nanda as the Chairman and Managing Director and Nikhil Nanda as the Managing Director.

candidates.title: Physicians Mutual
candidates.text: Physicians Mutual is a privately held insurance company headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, United States, that consists of Physicians Mutual Insurance Company and Physicians Life Insurance Company.

candidates.title: Physicians Mutual
candidates.text: Founded as Physicians Mutual Insurance Company in 1902 by Edwin E. Elliott, Physicians Mutual began by selling health insurance to medical professionals.

candidates.title: Physicians Mutual
candidates.text: Policies were offered to the general public starting in 1962, and by 1970 the company expanded into life insurance when it founded Physicians Life Insurance Company.

candidates.title: Physicians Mutual
candidates.text: Today the company offers a variety of insurance products, annuities, Medicare, Medigap, Medicare Supplement, Term Life Insurance, Whole Life Insurance, Cancer and funeral pre-planning services.

candidates.title: Physicians Mutual
candidates.text: It holds over US$3 billion in assets and employs over one thousand people.

candidates.title: Physicians Mutual
candidates.text: Robert A. Reed is chief executive officer and president.

candidates.title: Whole life insurance
candidates.text: Whole life insurance, or whole of life assurance (in the Commonwealth of Nations), sometimes called "straight life" or "ordinary life," is a life insurance policy which is guaranteed to remain in force for the insured's entire lifetime, provided required premiums are paid, or to the maturity date.

candidates.title: Whole life insurance
candidates.text: As a life insurance policy it represents a contract between the insured and insurer that as long as the contract terms are met, the insurer will pay the death benefit of the policy to the policy's beneficiaries when the insured dies.

candidates.title: Whole life insurance
candidates.text: Because whole life policies are guaranteed to remain in force as long as the required premiums are paid, the premiums are typically much higher than those of term life insurance where the premium is fixed only for a limited term.

candidates.title: Whole life insurance
candidates.text: Whole life premiums are fixed, based on the age of issue, and usually do not increase with age.

candidates.title: Whole life insurance
candidates.text: The insured party normally pays premiums until death, except for limited pay policies which may be paid-up in 10 years, 20 years, or at age 65.

candidates.title: Whole life insurance

claim: The sponsor of The Open Our Democracy Act of 2017 is the Democrat running for president in 2020 who currently holds Maryland’s 6th district in the US House of Representatives.
label: SUPPORTED

candidates.title: Will Brooke (businessman)
candidates.text: William W. Brooke (born April 5, 1957) is the executive vice president and managing partner of Harbert Management Corporation in Birmingham, Alabama.

candidates.title: Will Brooke (businessman)
candidates.text: He was one of seven candidates who ran for the Republican Party nomination in the 2014 US House of Representatives primary in the Alabama's 6th district, placing fifth.

candidates.title: Dave Bruderly
candidates.text: Dave Bruderly, an environmental engineering consultant who ran and lost against incumbent, Cliff Stearns (R), for Florida's 6th congressional district seat see Florida U.S. House election, 2006.

candidates.title: Dave Bruderly
candidates.text: He is a graduate of the United States Merchant Marine Academy in Marine Engineering and of Columbia University with an ocean engineering degree.

candidates.title: Dave Bruderly
candidates.text: Bruderly is a Democrat running in a six-county District that includes Alachua, Bradford, Clay, Duval, Lake, Levy, Marion and Gilchrist Counties.

candidates.title: Cuban Democracy Act
candidates.text: The Cuban Democracy Act was a bill presented by U.S. Congressman Robert Torricelli and passed in 1992 which prohibited foreign-based subsidiaries of U.S. companies from trading with Cuba, travel to Cuba by U.S. citizens, and family remittances to Cuba.

candidates.title: Cuban Democracy Act
candidates.text: The act was passed as “A bill to promote a peaceful transition to democracy in Cuba through the application of sanctions directed at the Castro government and support for the Cuban people.”

candidates.title: Cuban Democracy Act
candidates.text: The act stated that “[t]he government of Fidel Castro has demonstrated consistent disregard for internationally accepted standards of human rights and for democratic values” adding “[t]here is no sign that the Castro regime is prepared to make any significant concessions to democracy or to undertake any form of democratic opening.”

candidates.title: Cuban Democracy Act
candidates.text: Congressman Torricelli stated that the act was intended to "wreak havoc on that island."

candidates.title: Workplace Democracy Act of 1999
candidates.text: The Workplace Democracy Act of 1999 (HR 1277) was a proposed US labor law in the United States House of Representatives, sponsored by Bernie Sanders.

candidates.title: Workplace Democracy Act of 1999
candidates.text: It would have removed obstacles to employers making collective agreements, established an impartial National Public Employment Relations Commission to support fair collective bargaining, and required that pensions plans are jointly managed by employee and employer representatives.

candidates.title: Gar Alperovitz
candidates.text: Gar Alperovitz (born May 5, 1936) is an American political economist and historian.

candidates.title: Gar Alperovitz
candidates.text: He was the Lionel R. Bauman Professor of Political Economy at the University of Maryland, College Park Department of Government and Politics from 1999 to 2015.

candidates.title: Gar Alperovitz
candidates.text: Alperovitz was a Fellow of King's College, Cambridge; a founding Fellow of the Harvard Institute of Politics; a Fellow at the Institute for Policy Studies; and a Guest Scholar at the Brookings Institution.

candidates.title: Gar Alperovitz
candidates.text: He also served as a Legislative Director in the US House of Representatives and the US Senate and as a Special Assistant in the US Department of State.

candidates.title: Gar Alperovitz
candidates.text: Alperovitz is a member of the board of directors for the New Economics Institute and a founding principal of the Democracy Collaborative.

candidates.title: Gar Alperovitz
candidates.text: As of April 2015, he serves on the Green Shadow Cabinet of the United States as "New Economy Advisor to the President".

candidates.title: Maryland's 6th congressional district
candidates.text: Maryland's 6th congressional district elects a representative to the United States House of Representatives from the northwest part of the state.

candidates.title: Maryland's 6th congressional district
candidates.text: Today the district comprises all of Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties as well as portions of Montgomery and Frederick counties.

candidates.title: Maryland's 6th congressional district
candidates.text: The seat is currently represented by John Delaney (D).

candidates.title: John Delaney (Maryland politician)
candidates.text: John Kevin Delaney (born April 16, 1963) is an American politician and businessman who has been the United States Representative for Maryland's 6th congressional district since 2013 and is running for President of the United States in 2020.

candidates.title: John Delaney (Maryland politician)
candidates.text: The district, the state's second-largest, includes nearly the entire western portion of the state, but the bulk of its vote is cast in the outer suburbs of Washington, D.C.

candidates.title: John Delaney (Maryland politician)
candidates.text: He is a member of the Democratic Party.

candidates.title: Open Our Democracy Act of 2017
candidates.text: The Open Our Democracy Act of 2017 (H.R. 2981 of the 115th congress) is a bill sponsored by Rep. John Delaney which would establish Election Day as a federal holiday, mandate all congressional primary elections to be open elections so all eligible voters can participate in them, and end gerrymandering by requiring independent commissions to draw the districts in each state.

claim: James Munyala, one of the runners who almost broke Illinois Boys Cross Country record was born in Lithuania. The runner who had the record also suggested these athletes displaced opportunities for American athletes.
label: SUPPORTED

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: James Munyala (born November 2, 1952) is a Kenyan athlete, known for running the steeplechase.

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: Running for the University of Texas, El Paso he won three straight NCAA Championships 1975-1977.

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: His 1976 win set the Franklin Field record that stood for 32 years.

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: He was part of the controversial beginning wave of imported, older Kenyan athletes who allowed UTEP and Washington State University to dominate NCAA distance running.

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: At the time, Craig Virgin suggested these athletes displaced opportunities for American athletes.

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: Another star athlete mentioned was Washington State's Henry Rono who succeeded Munyala as NCAA Champion, with Munyala as runner-up, in 1978, blocking his attempt to win four straight.

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: Later in 1978, Rono and Munyala went 1-2 for Kenya at both the African Games and the Commonwealth Games.

candidates.title: James Munyala
candidates.text: Munyala won the Indoor Mile for UTEP in 1978 and is in the university's Hall of Fame when they ran the triple crown of the Men's Indoor, Outdoor and Cross Country Championships all in the same year.

candidates.title: Craig Virgin
candidates.text: Craig Steven Virgin (born August 2, 1955) is an American distance runner.

candidates.title: Craig Virgin
candidates.text: He was born in Belleville, Illinois and grew up near Lebanon, Illinois.

candidates.title: Craig Virgin
candidates.text: While in high school, Virgin won 5 state championships (two in cross country and three in track) as well as setting the national outdoor high school 2-mile record of 8:40.9 (beating Steve Prefontaine's mark of 8:41.5, though slightly short of Gerry Lindgren's 8:40.0 indoor record from 1964).

candidates.title: Craig Virgin
candidates.text: Additionally, Virgin remains the record-holder in Illinois Boys Cross Country, running a 13:50.6 in 1972, which has only been approached by within five seconds by Chris Derrick in 2007 (13:51.8) and Lukas Verzbicas in 2010 (13:53.8).

candidates.title: Craig Virgin
candidates.text: He was "Track and Field News" "High School Athlete of the Year" in 1973.

candidates.title: Tim Broe
candidates.text: Tim Broe (born June 20, 1977 in Peoria, Illinois) is a retired American long-distance runner.

candidates.title: Tim Broe
candidates.text: He reached the 5000 meters final at the 2004 Summer Olympics finishing eleventh.

candidates.title: Tim Broe
candidates.text: Tim competed collegiately for the University of Alabama where his 3,000m steeplechase record still stands.

candidates.title: Tim Broe
candidates.text: He is a cross country running and track and field coach.

candidates.title: Tim Broe
candidates.text: In his second year of coaching Wellesley High School boys cross country, the team won the MIAA Division State Cross Country Championships

candidates.title: Pan American Cross Country Cup
candidates.text: The Pan American Cross Country Cup ("Copa Panamericana de Cross Country") is an international Cross country running competition organized by the Association of Panamerican Athletics (APA) for athletes representing the countries and territories of its member associations.

candidates.title: Pan American Cross Country Cup
candidates.text: It was established in 2015.

candidates.title: Pan American Cross Country Cup
candidates.text: Races are featured for senior, junior (U-20) and youth (U-18) athletes.

candidates.title: Pan American Cross Country Cup
candidates.text: The inaugural 2015 edition in Barranquilla, Colombia simultaneously serves as NACAC Cross Country Championships and South American Cross Country Championships.

candidates.title: 2012 African Cross Country Championships
candidates.text: The 2nd African Cross Country Championships was an international cross country running competition for African athletes which was held on 18 March 2012 in Cape Town's Keurboom Park in South Africa.

candidates.title: 2012 African Cross Country Championships
candidates.text: Organised by the Confederation of African Athletics and Athletics South Africa, it was the first time that the competition represented that year's foremost event in the sport, as the IAAF World Cross Country Championships was not held.

candidates.title: 2012 African Cross Country Championships
candidates.text: Twenty-one nations entered athletes into the event and 160 runners participated in the races.

candidates.title: Lukas Verzbicas
candidates.text: Lukas Verzbicas (born "Lukas Veržbickas" January 6, 1993 in Kaunas, Lithuania) is a Lithuanian-American triathlete.

candidates.title: Lukas Verzbicas
candidates.text: A prominent high school track and cross country runner, Verzbicas holds the U.S. high school national record in the 2 mile with a time of 8:29.46.

candidates.title: Lukas Verzbicas
candidates.text: He was also the fifth of only nine American high school boys to run a sub four-minute mile, running 3:59.71 at the end of his senior year of high school.

claim:
The CGI animated series, that preceded the Cartoon Network series with Brian Stepanek as Magnifo,  
 first aired on January 16, 2013.
label: SUPPORTED

candidates.title: Brian Stepanek
candidates.text: Brian Patrick Stepanek (born February 6, 1971) is an American actor and voice actor.

candidates.title: Brian Stepanek
candidates.text: He is known for his role as Arwin Hawkhauser on the Disney Channel Original Series "The Suite Life of Zack & Cody" and Brian on "Brian O'Brian".

candidates.title: Brian Stepanek
candidates.text: He was also a Sector Seven Agent in the 2007 Michael Bay film "Transformers", and also had a supporting role in "The Island".

candidates.title: Brian Stepanek
candidates.text: He is now known for playing Tom Harper on the Nickelodeon series "Nicky, Ricky, Dicky & Dawn"; the voice of Lynn Loud Sr. on the Nickelodeon animated series "The Loud House"; and as the voice of Magnifo on the shortform Cartoon Network series "Mixels".

candidates.title: Hot Wheels Battle Force 5
candidates.text: Hot Wheels Battle Force 5 is an American—Canadian 3D CGI animated television series created by Mattel, Nelvana Limited, and Nerd Corps Entertainment, based on the Hot Wheels toy line by the American toy maker Mattel which was introduced in 1968.

candidates.title: Hot Wheels Battle Force 5
candidates.text: A two-episode preview aired on Cartoon Network in the United States on August 24, 2009; it was shown on Cartoon Network India starting on April 30, 2010 and on Cartoon Network Philippines from July 3, 2010.

candidates.title: Hot Wheels Battle Force 5
candidates.text: The series made its official debut on August 29.

candidates.title: Hot Wheels Battle Force 5
candidates.text: According to a HotWheels.com page as of July 14, 2010 describing "BATTLE FORCE 5 Battle Action Assortment" toys, vehicles combine forces to create even more powerful combat machines.

candidates.title: Hot Wheels Battle Force 5
candidates.text: The second season began airing September 18, 2010.

candidates.title: Cartoon Network (Middle East and Africa)
candidates.text: Cartoon Network refers to two digital children's TV channels broadcasting animated programs: Cartoon Network MENA, which serves the Middle East and North Africa region (excluding Israel, Iran and Turkey) along with Cyprus; and Cartoon Network Africa (formerly known as Cartoon Network HQ), which serves Sub-Saharan Africa.

candidates.title: Cartoon Network (Middle East and Africa)
candidates.text: Cartoon Network was created by Turner Broadcasting System, a unit of Time Warner.

candidates.title: Cartoon Network (Middle East and Africa)
candidates.text: Cartoon Network UK/Europe (the direct precursor to Cartoon Network feeds in the EMEA region, including Cartoon Network HQ) was launched on September 17, 1993.

candidates.title: Cartoon Network (Middle East and Africa)
candidates.text: In October 1999, Cartoon Network UK became a separate feed from Cartoon Network HQ, but initially had a nearly identical schedule to Cartoon Network HQ until the latter became completely independent from the UK feed in 2001.

candidates.title: Out of Jimmy's Head
candidates.text: Out of Jimmy's Head (abbreviated as OOJH), is an American live-action/animated television series.

candidates.title: Out of Jimmy's Head
candidates.text: It was advertised as the first Cartoon Network series in this genre, even though "Big Bag" was what took credit, while also including some animated segments.

candidates.title: Out of Jimmy's Head
candidates.text: Based on the first live-action/animated original channel movie "Re-Animated", that was aired on December 8, 2006, it is produced by Cartoon Network Studios and Brookwell McNamara Entertainment (the latter known for shows such as "Even Stevens" and "That's So Raven").

candidates.title: Out of Jimmy's Head
candidates.text: It was created by Tim McKeon and Adam Pava, who were originally the writers for "Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends" and "The Life and Times of Juniper Lee", but also the creators of "Weighty Decisions" short on Cartoon Network's "Sunday Pants" anthology series.

candidates.title: Mixels
candidates.text: Mixels was a 2014 comedy animated television series that aired on Cartoon Network, co-produced by The Lego Group and Cartoon Network Studios.

candidates.title: Mixels
candidates.text: The series first aired on February 12, 2014 with a new episode of "Teen Titans Go!"

candidates.title: Mixels
candidates.text: The series revolves around the Mixels, small creatures that can mix and combine with one another in creative and unpredictable storylines.

candidates.title: Mixels
candidates.text: Although previous Lego series, such as "" and "Legends of Chima" use CGI animation, "Mixels" made use of Toon Boom Harmony software, which is animated at Atomic Cartoons, Inc., before later being animated traditionally at Digital eMation, Inc., Big Star Entertainment, Inc., and Saerom Animation, Inc.

candidates.title: Legends of Chima
candidates.text: Legends of Chima is a CGI animated television series based on the LEGO Legends of Chima series of LEGO sets.

candidates.title: Legends of Chima
candidates.text: It began with 2 episodes airing on January 16, 2013, with the Season 1 finale on December 5, 2013.

claim: Vic & Anthony's Steakhouse is located at the American casino that was combined with the California Club. The casino is owned by Landry's, Inc.
label: SUPPORTED

candidates.title: California Club (casino)
candidates.text: The California Club operated from 1958 to 1973.

candidates.title: California Club (casino)
candidates.text: Phil Long took over operation of the casino located at the corner of First and Fremont Street in Downtown Las Vegas, Nevada, 1958.

candidates.title: California Club (casino)
candidates.text: The locals casino catered to local gamblers.

candidates.title: California Club (casino)
candidates.text: It was owned and operated by Phil Long and partner George Milford and was a casino only without any hotel rooms.

candidates.title: California Club (casino)
candidates.text: The California Club was sold to Steve Wynn in 1973.

candidates.title: California Club (casino)
candidates.text: The California Club was combined into the Golden Nugget shortly after the purchase by Wynn.

candidates.title: Gold Mountain Casino
candidates.text: Gold Mountain Casino is a Native American casino in Ardmore, Oklahoma, owned and operated by the Chickasaw Nation.

candidates.title: Gold Mountain Casino
candidates.text: Originally opened in 2002 as Ardmore Gaming, the facility has grown steadily and today features more than 300 gaming machines.

candidates.title: Gold Mountain Casino
candidates.text: The casino is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

candidates.title: Gold Mountain Casino
candidates.text: The 8620 sqft casino is located on the corner of P Street N.E. and Sam Noble Parkway, and can be accessed via Interstate 35, exit 33.

candidates.title: Gold Mountain Casino
candidates.text: It is a short distance from the Ardmore Convention Center and the Hardy Murphy Coliseum.

candidates.title: Gold Mountain Casino
candidates.text: Gold Mountain is about 34 miles north of WinStar World Casino in Thackerville, Oklahoma, and 77 miles south of Riverwind Casino in Norman, Oklahoma, which are also Chickasaw-owned gaming facilities.

candidates.title: Blackbird Bend Casino
candidates.text: Blackbird Bend Casino, formerly CasinOmaha, is a Native American casino located in Onawa, Iowa.

candidates.title: Blackbird Bend Casino
candidates.text: The casino was first opened in July 1992 as CasinOmaha, and was shuttered for renovations in 2009.

candidates.title: Blackbird Bend Casino
candidates.text: On 15 October 2010, it was reopened under its new name, but on 2 June 2011 the casino was shut down due to extensive flooding damage as a result of the 2011 Missouri River Flood.

candidates.title: Blackbird Bend Casino
candidates.text: The casino reopened April 2013.

candidates.title: Blackbird Bend Casino
candidates.text: The casino features 340 separate gaming machines, and tables for poker, craps, blackjack, and roulette.

candidates.title: Blackbird Bend Casino
candidates.text: Live music is offered on weekends, and a number of retail shops are available in the casino.

candidates.title: Vic & Anthony's Steakhouse
candidates.text: Vic & Anthony’s is an American steakhouse restaurant chain with locations in Downtown Houston, ]and inside the Golden Nugget Casinos in Las Vegas and Atlantic City.

candidates.title: Vic & Anthony's Steakhouse
candidates.text: A fourth location is scheduled to open inside the new Golden Nugget Lake Charles in late 2014.

candidates.title: Vic & Anthony's Steakhouse
candidates.text: Vic & Anthony’s is owned and operated by Landry’s, Inc.

candidates.title: Meskwaki Casino
candidates.text: Meskwaki Casino is a Native American casino located in Tama, Iowa.

candidates.title: Meskwaki Casino
candidates.text: It is owned and operated by the Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa, and opened in 1992.

candidates.title: Meskwaki Casino
candidates.text: The casino consists of 127,669 sq. ft. of gaming space, filled by tables for stud poker, blackjack, craps, baccarat, roulette, hold 'em, and others.

candidates.title: Meskwaki Casino
candidates.text: Also available are slot machines, keno, bingo, and the sportsbook.

candidates.title: Meskwaki Casino
candidates.text: The casino abuts a 404-room resort hotel.

candidates.title: Golden Nugget Las Vegas
candidates.text: The Golden Nugget Las Vegas is a luxury hotel and casino located in Las Vegas, Nevada on the Fremont Street Experience.

candidates.title: Golden Nugget Las Vegas
candidates.text: The property is owned and operated by Landry's, Inc.

claim: The Wien Liesing railway station opened in the same year as this railway, It runs from Vienna to Graz and the border with Slovenia at Spielfeld via the first mountain railway built in Europe to use standard gauge track.
label: SUPPORTED

candidates.title: Semmering railway
candidates.text: The Semmering railway (German: "Semmeringbahn" ) in Austria, which starts at Gloggnitz and leads over the Semmering to Mürzzuschlag was the first mountain railway in Europe built with a standard gauge track.

candidates.title: Semmering railway
candidates.text: It is commonly referred to as the world's first true mountain railway, given the very difficult terrain and the considerable altitude difference that was mastered during its construction.

candidates.title: Semmering railway
candidates.text: It is still fully functional as a part of the Southern Railway which is operated by the Austrian Federal Railways.

candidates.title: Southern Railway (Austria)
candidates.text: The Southern Railway (German: "Südbahn" ) is a railway in Austria that runs from Vienna to Graz and the border with Slovenia at Spielfeld via Semmering and Bruck an der Mur.

candidates.title: Southern Railway (Austria)
candidates.text: It was originally built by the Austrian Southern Railway company and ran to Ljubljana and Trieste, the main seaport of the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy.

candidates.title: Southern Railway (Austria)
candidates.text: The twin-track, electrified section that runs through the current territory of Austria is owned and operated by Austrian Federal Railways (ÖBB) and is one of the major lines in the country.

candidates.title: Wien Liesing railway station
candidates.text: Wien Liesing is a railway station in the 23 district of Vienna.

candidates.title: Wien Liesing railway station
candidates.text: The station is located 7 km southwest of Meidling station and is served by S-Bahn and most ÖBB Regional trains.

candidates.title: Wien Liesing railway station
candidates.text: The station was opened in 1841 along with the Southern Railway.

candidates.title: Wien Liesing railway station
candidates.text: The history Liesing brewery has been converted in 2010 to a shopping mall and is one block west of the station.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: The Catalan Talgo was an international express train introduced in 1969 that linked Geneva, Switzerland, with Barcelona, Spain.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: It was named after the Spanish region Catalonia and the Talgo equipment it used.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: It was an extension and upgrading of a predecessor train, "Le Catalan", a first-class-only French (SNCF) "Rapide" train that had been in operation since 1955 but running only between Geneva and the stations nearest the Spanish-French border, connecting with a second-class-only "autorail" trainset to and from Barcelona.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: The national railway network of Spain, "Red Nacional de los Ferrocarriles Españoles" (RENFE), was using Iberian gauge for all of its main lines, while those of France and Switzerland use standard gauge.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: As a result of this break-of-gauge, train journeys between Geneva and Barcelona consisted of two separate parts, with travelers having to change from a French to a Spanish train or vice versa at the border—at Portbou (alternatively written as Port Bou) on southbound trains and at Cerbère on northbound trains.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: In 1968, this was resolved with the introduction of the Talgo III RD trainsets, which featured variable gauge wheelsets.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: At Portbou station, the wheel spacing of each passenger carriage was adjusted by a gauge changer for the difference in gauge, and passengers no longer had to change trains.

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: After successful test runs, the "Catalan" was extended from Port Bou to Barcelona as a through train on 1 June 1969, becoming the "Catalan Talgo" and upgraded to a Trans Europ Express (TEE).

candidates.title: Catalan Talgo
candidates.text: Most other rail journeys through this border crossing continued to require a change of train at Cerbère station or at Port Bou, as most trains did not use Talgo III RD trainsets.

candidates.title: Mombasa–Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
candidates.text: The Mombasa–Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway (SGR) is a standard gauge railway that connects the port city of Mombasa to Kenya's capital city Nairobi.

candidates.title: Mombasa–Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
candidates.text: The railway replaces the parallel metre-gauge railway that was originally built by the British in the 19th century.

candidates.title: Mombasa–Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
candidates.text: Under the East African Railway Master Plan, the Mombasa–Nairobi SGR will link up with other standard gauge railways that are being built in East Africa.

candidates.title: Mombasa–Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway
candidates.text: Construction is already under way on Phase II of the Kenya SGR, which will extend the railway to the Uganda border by 2021.

claim: The President that Jefferson County, Oklahoma was named in honor of, was an American Founding Father, a proponent of democracy, republicanism, and individual rights, who examined Ice Age fossils of Kentucky's Big Bone Lick.
label: SUPPORTED
documents: History of paleontology in the United States
tfidf_top5_documents: History of paleontology in the United States

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The history of paleontology in the United States refers to the developments and discoveries regarding fossils found within or by people from the United States of America.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: Local paleontology began informally with Native Americans, who have been familiar with fossils for thousands of years.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: They both told myths about them and applied them to practical purposes.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: African slaves also contributed their knowledge; the first reasonably accurate recorded identification of vertebrate fossils in the new world was made by slaves on a South Carolina plantation who recognized the elephant affinities of mammoth molars uncovered there in 1725.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The first major fossil discovery to attract the attention of formally trained scientists were the Ice Age fossils of Kentucky's Big Bone Lick.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: These fossils were studied by eminent intellectuals like France's George Cuvier and local statesmen and frontiersman like Daniel Boone, Benjamin Franklin, William Henry Harrison, Thomas Jefferson, and George Washington.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: By the end of the 18th century possible dinosaur fossils had already been found.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Big Bone Lick State Park is located at Big Bone in Boone County, Kentucky.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The name of the park comes from the Pleistocene megafauna fossils found there.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Mammoths are believed to have been drawn to this location by a salt lick deposited around sulphur springs.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Other animals including forms of bison, caribou, deer, elk, horse, mastodon, moose, musk ox, peccary, sloth, and possibly tapir also grazed the vegetation and salty earth around the springs that the animals relied on for their diet.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The area near the springs was very soft and marshy causing many animals to become stuck with no way to escape.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: It bills itself as "the birthplace of American paleontology", a term which dates from the 1807 expedition by William Clark undertaken at the direction of President Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In Nicholas Cresswell's journal, dated 1774 to 1777, he records a visit in 1775 to what was then called "Elephant Bone Lick."

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In this account, Cresswell describes finding several bones of "prodigious size", as well as tusk fragments, and teeth—one weighing approximately 10 pounds.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: While he assumed the bones were from ancient elephants, the local native traditions claimed the bones to be those of white buffaloes that had been poisoned by the salty water.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Paleontology in Kentucky refers to paleontological research occurring within or conducted by people from the U.S. state of Kentucky.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Kentucky's abundance of exposed sedimentary rock makes it an ideal source of fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The oldest exposed rocks in Kentucky are of Ordovician age.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The geologic column of Kentucky also contains rocks deposited during the ensuing periods until the end of the Pennsylvanian.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During this span of time the state was first home to a warm shallow sea home to an abundance and variety of brachiopods, cephalopods, crinoids, and trilobites.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During the Devonian, a large reef system formed at what is now the Falls of the Ohio.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Swamps covered Kentucky during the ensuing Carboniferous period.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Then a gap spans from the start of the Permian to the Pleistocene, although the gap is interrupted by minor deposits of Cretaceous and Eocene rocks.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: These deposits mainly preserve plant fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Ice Age Kentucky was home to short-faced bear, bison, elk, lions, mammoths, mastodons, and giant ground sloths.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Local Native Americans interpreted fossils of this age at Big Bone Lick as belonging to ancient monsters killed by benevolent mystical little people.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: This same fossil deposit would attract attention from major American figures like George Washington, Daniel Boone, and, especially, Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Amateur fossil collectors should be aware that they need permission from landowners to prospect legally on private property.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Brachiopods are the Kentucky state fossil.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: Big Bone is an unincorporated community in southern Boone County, Kentucky, United States.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The history of paleontology in the United States refers to the developments and discoveries regarding fossils found within or by people from the United States of America.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: Local paleontology began informally with Native Americans, who have been familiar with fossils for thousands of years.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: They both told myths about them and applied them to practical purposes.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: African slaves also contributed their knowledge; the first reasonably accurate recorded identification of vertebrate fossils in the new world was made by slaves on a South Carolina plantation who recognized the elephant affinities of mammoth molars uncovered there in 1725.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The first major fossil discovery to attract the attention of formally trained scientists were the Ice Age fossils of Kentucky's Big Bone Lick.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: These fossils were studied by eminent intellectuals like France's George Cuvier and local statesmen and frontiersman like Daniel Boone, Benjamin Franklin, William Henry Harrison, Thomas Jefferson, and George Washington.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: By the end of the 18th century possible dinosaur fossils had already been found.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Big Bone Lick State Park is located at Big Bone in Boone County, Kentucky.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The name of the park comes from the Pleistocene megafauna fossils found there.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Mammoths are believed to have been drawn to this location by a salt lick deposited around sulphur springs.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Other animals including forms of bison, caribou, deer, elk, horse, mastodon, moose, musk ox, peccary, sloth, and possibly tapir also grazed the vegetation and salty earth around the springs that the animals relied on for their diet.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The area near the springs was very soft and marshy causing many animals to become stuck with no way to escape.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: It bills itself as "the birthplace of American paleontology", a term which dates from the 1807 expedition by William Clark undertaken at the direction of President Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In Nicholas Cresswell's journal, dated 1774 to 1777, he records a visit in 1775 to what was then called "Elephant Bone Lick."

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In this account, Cresswell describes finding several bones of "prodigious size", as well as tusk fragments, and teeth—one weighing approximately 10 pounds.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: While he assumed the bones were from ancient elephants, the local native traditions claimed the bones to be those of white buffaloes that had been poisoned by the salty water.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Paleontology in Kentucky refers to paleontological research occurring within or conducted by people from the U.S. state of Kentucky.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Kentucky's abundance of exposed sedimentary rock makes it an ideal source of fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The oldest exposed rocks in Kentucky are of Ordovician age.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The geologic column of Kentucky also contains rocks deposited during the ensuing periods until the end of the Pennsylvanian.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During this span of time the state was first home to a warm shallow sea home to an abundance and variety of brachiopods, cephalopods, crinoids, and trilobites.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During the Devonian, a large reef system formed at what is now the Falls of the Ohio.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Swamps covered Kentucky during the ensuing Carboniferous period.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Then a gap spans from the start of the Permian to the Pleistocene, although the gap is interrupted by minor deposits of Cretaceous and Eocene rocks.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: These deposits mainly preserve plant fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Ice Age Kentucky was home to short-faced bear, bison, elk, lions, mammoths, mastodons, and giant ground sloths.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Local Native Americans interpreted fossils of this age at Big Bone Lick as belonging to ancient monsters killed by benevolent mystical little people.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: This same fossil deposit would attract attention from major American figures like George Washington, Daniel Boone, and, especially, Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Amateur fossil collectors should be aware that they need permission from landowners to prospect legally on private property.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Brachiopods are the Kentucky state fossil.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
