candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: The northern extent is along Hathaway Road, and the eastern portion extends not further than U.S. 42, and is approached from that direction by Beaver Road (Route 338) coming from either Richwood or Walton.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: Big Bone took its name from a nearby prehistoric mineral lick of the same name.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky

candidates.title: Thomas Jefferson
candidates.text: Thomas Jefferson (April 13 [O.S. April 2] 1743 – July 4, 1826) was an American Founding Father who was the principal author of the Declaration of Independence and later served as the third President of the United States from 1801 to 1809.

candidates.title: Thomas Jefferson

candidates.title: History of the Calvinist–Arminian debate
candidates.text: The history of the Calvinist–Arminian debate begins in early 17th century in the Netherlands with a Christian theological dispute between the followers of John Calvin and Jacobus Arminius, and continues today among some Protestants, particularly evangelicals.

candidates.title: History of the Calvinist–Arminian debate
candidates.text: The debate centers around soteriology, or the study of salvation, and includes disputes about total depravity, predestination, and atonement.

candidates.title: History of the Calvinist–Arminian debate
candidates.text: While the debate was given its Calvinist-Arminian form in the 17th Century, issues central to the debate have been discussed in Christianity in some form since Augustine of Hippo's disputes with the Pelagians in the 5th century.

candidates.title: Arminianism
candidates.text: Arminianism is based on theological ideas of the Dutch Reformed theologian Jacobus Arminius (1560–1609) and his historic supporters known as Remonstrants.

candidates.title: Arminianism
candidates.text: His teachings held to the five solae of the Reformation, but they were distinct from particular teachings of Martin Luther, Huldrych Zwingli, John Calvin, and other Protestant Reformers.

candidates.title: Arminianism
candidates.text: Jacobus Arminius (Jakob Harmenszoon) was a student of Theodore Beza (Calvin's successor) at the Theological University of Geneva.

candidates.title: Arminianism
candidates.text: Arminianism is known to some as a soteriological diversification of Protestant Calvinist Christianity.

candidates.title: Arminianism
candidates.text: However, to others, Arminianism is a reclamation of early Church theological consensus.

candidates.text: It is associated with John Calvin, Theodore Beza and John Knox.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Pieter Datheen, Latin Petrus Dathenus, English, Peter Datheen, (Cassel, Nord, c.1531 - Elbing, 17 March 1588) was a Dutch Calvinist theologian who accomplished many things for the advancement the Reformed Church liturgy.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: First, he translated the Heidelberg Catechism into Dutch.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Second, using the singing work of John Calvin,Theodore Beza, Peter Marot, and Louis Bourgeois, Datheen set the Psalms and psalter to verse and tune in Dutch (1566), though his settings were overshadowed by those of Philips Marnix van St Aldegonde.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Third, he wrote the famous "Form for the Administration of Holy Baptism" with its very orthodox emphasis on the Covenant of Grace containing two parts.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Fourth, he wrote the equally famous "Form for the Administration of the Lord's Supper" still used by orthodox Reformed churches today.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Fifth, he was President of the Convent of Wesel in 1568, which expressed hope for the Reformed Churches to be free from the awful persecution of Spanish Roman Catholics, and more significantly President of the 1578 Synod of Dordt.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Sixth, at this latter Synod he helped write, edit, and approve the long-revered Church Order (more famously known as the 1618-1619 Church Order of Dordt) with its 84 articles.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Seventh, he developed the liturgy (order of worship) used by orthodox Dutch and American Reformed Churches with the singing, alms, prayer, and preaching at the required places.

candidates.title: Petrus Dathenus
candidates.text: Eighth and finally, during Roman Catholic Spain's very intense persecution of the Lowlands region, resulting in the deaths of 100,000 - 200,000 Reformed Christians, Datheen was a field preacher carrying his pulpit on his back and then orating to crowds of 15,000 in a blunt eloquence that was intense and captivating.

candidates.title: Jacobus Arminius
candidates.text: He wrote many books and treatises on theology, and his views became the basis of Arminianism and the Dutch Remonstrant movement.

candidates.title: Hand of God (art)
candidates.text: The Hand of God, or Manus Dei in Latin, also known as Dextera domini/dei, the "right hand of God", is a motif in Jewish and Christian art, especially of the Late Antique and Early Medieval periods, when depiction of Jehovah or God the Father as a full human figure was considered unacceptable.

candidates.title: Hand of God (art)
candidates.text: The hand, sometimes including a portion of an arm, or ending about the wrist, is used to indicate the intervention in or approval of affairs on Earth by God, and sometimes as a subject in itself.

candidates.title: Hand of God (art)
candidates.text: It is an artistic metaphor that is generally not intended to indicate that a hand was physically present or seen at any subject depicted.

candidates.title: Hand of God (art)
candidates.text: The Hand is seen appearing from above in a fairly restricted number of narrative contexts, often in a blessing gesture (in Christian examples), but sometimes performing an action.

candidates.title: Hand of God (art)
candidates.text: In later Christian works it tends to be replaced by a fully realized figure of God the Father, whose depiction had become acceptable in Western Christianity, although not in Eastern Orthodox or Jewish art.

candidates.title: Hand of God (art)
candidates.text: Though the hand of God has traditionally been understood as a symbol for God's intervention or approval of human affairs, it is also possible that the hand of God reflects the anthropomorphic conceptions of the deity that may have persisted in late antiquity.

candidates.title: Pensive Christ
candidates.text: The Pensive Christ or Christus im Elend ("Christ in Distress" in German) or Christus in der Rast or Chrystus Frasobliwy ("Christ Sorrowful" in Polish) is a subject in Christian iconography depicting a contemplating Jesus, sitting with his head supported by his hand with the Crown of Thorns and marks of his flagellation.

candidates.title: Pensive Christ
candidates.text: It is therefore a picture of Jesus shortly before his crucifixion, although more an andachtsbild or devotional subject than intended to show an actual moment in the narrative of the Passion of Christ.

candidates.title: Pensive Christ
candidates.text: The Pensive Christ is much more common in sculpture than in painting, where the similar Man of Sorrows is more often depicted (in this Jesus is shown with the wounds of the crucifixion).

candidates.title: Madonna of the Yarnwinder

candidates.title: Madonna of the Yarnwinder
candidates.text: Leonardo was recorded as being at work on one such picture in Florence in 1501 for Florimond Robertet, a secretary to King Louis XII of France.

candidates.title: Madonna of the Yarnwinder
candidates.text: This may have been delivered to the French court in 1507, though scholars are divided on this point.

candidates.title: Madonna of the Yarnwinder
candidates.text: The subject is known today from several versions of which two, called the Buccleuch Madonna and the Lansdowne Madonna, are thought to be partly by Leonardo’s hand.

candidates.title: Madonna of the Yarnwinder
candidates.text: The underdrawings of both paintings show similar experimental changes made to the composition (or "pentimenti"), suggesting that both evolved concurrently in Leonardo’s workshop.

candidates.title: Tone Clock
candidates.text: The Tone Clock, and its related compositional theory Tone-Clock Theory, is a post-tonal music composition technique, developed by composers Peter Schat and Jenny McLeod.

candidates.title: Tone Clock
candidates.text: Music written using tone-clock theory features a high economy of musical intervals within a generally chromatic musical language.

candidates.title: Tone Clock
candidates.text: This is because tone-clock theory encourages the composer to generate all their harmonic and melodic material from a limited number of intervallic configurations (called 'Intervallic Prime Forms', or IPFs, in tone-clock terminology).

candidates.title: Tone Clock
candidates.text: Tone-clock theory is also concerned with the way that the three-note pitch-class sets (trichords or 'triads' in tone-clock terminology) can be shown to underlie larger sets, and considers these triads as a fundamental unit in the harmonic world of any piece.

candidates.title: Tone Clock
candidates.text: Because there are twelve possible triadic prime forms, Schat called them the 'hours', and imagined them arrayed in a clock face, with the smallest hour (012 or 1-1 in IPF notation) in the 1 o'clock position, and the largest hour (048 or 4-4 in IPF notation) in the 12 o'clock position.

candidates.title: Tone Clock
candidates.text: A notable feature of Tone-Clock Theory is 'tone-clock steering': transposing and/or inverting hours so that each note of the chromatic aggregate is generated once and once only.

candidates.text: Electronics are the fastest growing trash group on the planet.

candidates.text: It is estimated that 41.8 million metric tonnes (Mt) of electronic waste were produced in 2014 alone.

candidates.text: The issue is that electronic devices are one of the only items disposed of even if they are not broken or defective.

candidates.title: Effects of cobalt from lithium ion batteries
candidates.text: In the case of current technology, new is already old.

candidates.title: Effects of cobalt from lithium ion batteries
candidates.text: Items that become obsolete are as susceptible to being thrown as ones that are broken.

candidates.title: Effects of cobalt from lithium ion batteries

candidates.title: Chevrolet
candidates.text: Chevrolet ( ), colloquially referred to as Chevy and formally the Chevrolet Division of General Motors Company, is an American automobile division of the American manufacturer General Motors (GM).

candidates.title: Chevrolet
candidates.text: Louis Chevrolet and ousted General Motors founder William C. Durant started the company on November 3, 1911 as the Chevrolet Motor Car Company.

candidates.title: Chevrolet
candidates.text: Durant used the Chevrolet Motor Car Company to acquire a controlling stake in General Motors with a reverse merger occurring on May 2, 1918 and propelled himself back to the GM presidency.

candidates.title: Chevrolet
candidates.text: After Durant's second ousting in 1919, Alfred Sloan, with his maxim "a car for every purse and purpose," would pick the Chevrolet brand to become the volume leader in the General Motors family, selling mainstream vehicles to compete with Henry Ford's Model T in 1919 and overtaking Ford as the best-selling car in the United States by 1929.

candidates.title: Chevrolet Opala
candidates.text: The Chevrolet Opala was a Brazilian mid-size car sold under the Chevrolet brand in South America from 1969 to 1992, by General Motors do Brasil.

candidates.title: Chevrolet Opala
candidates.text: It was derived from the German Opel Rekord Series C, Opel Commodore Series A, but used USA-sourced engines and Holden styling.

candidates.title: Chevrolet Opala
candidates.text: Two four-cylinder engines: the Chevrolet 153ci 4-cylinder from Chevy II/Nova, which later got a new crankshaft stroke and cylinder bore, changing its size to 151ci (usually mistaken for the Pontiac Iron Duke engine), and the six-cylinder 250 from the contemporary line of North American car/light truck production.

candidates.title: Chevrolet Opala
candidates.text: GM manufactured about one million units including the Opala sedan, Opala Coupé, and the station wagon variant, the Opala Caravan.

candidates.title: Chevrolet Opala
candidates.text: It was replaced by the Chevrolet Omega in 1992, also an Opel spinoff.

candidates.title: Chevrolet Opala
candidates.text: It was the first passenger car built by GM in Brazil by the General Motors do Brasil division.

candidates.title: Chevrolet Opala
candidates.text: A luxury version of the Opala was marketed as the Chevrolet Diplomata.

candidates.title: Samantha Larson

candidates.title: Peter Hillary
candidates.text: Peter Edmund Hillary (born 26 December 1954) is a New Zealand mountaineer, philanthropist and writer.

candidates.title: Peter Hillary
candidates.text: He is the son of adventurer Sir Edmund Hillary, who, along with Nepalese Sherpa mountain climber Tenzing Norgay, completed the first successful ascent of Mount Everest.

candidates.title: Peter Hillary
candidates.text: When Peter Hillary summited Everest in 1990, he and his father were the first father/son duo to achieve the feat.

candidates.title: Peter Hillary

candidates.title: Peter Hillary

candidates.title: Garrett Madison
candidates.text: Garrett Madison (born November 3, 1978) is an American mountaineer and is one of the world's top high altitude mountaineering guides, having personally guided 44 clients to the summit of Mt Everest between the years 2006-2016, more than any other American.

candidates.title: Garrett Madison
candidates.text: Garrett began guiding professionally in 1999 on Mount Rainier, and his company, Madison Mountaineering, specializes in leading expedition climbs on Mount Everest and other high altitude peaks, operates on the highest peaks on all seven continents (7 summits), and also provides domestic training programs and summit climbs in Washington State.

candidates.title: Garrett Madison
candidates.text: On May 19–20, 2011, he reached the summit of Mt Everest on his fourth successful attempt as expedition leader and guide for Alpine Ascents International, and reached the summit of Lhotse (4th highest mountain in the world) only 21 hours later as guide to climber Tom Halliday.

candidates.title: Garrett Madison
candidates.text: Also on the expedition was guide Michael Horst who made both summits as well in under a 24-hour period, a few days earlier.

candidates.title: Garrett Madison
candidates.text: This historic achievement marks the first time in history that both peaks Mt Everest and Lhotse were summited together in less than 24 hours, and Madison repeated the "double header" feat again in 2013, the only person to do so twice.

candidates.title: Garrett Madison

candidates.title: Garrett Madison

candidates.text: Jovan Šević or Ivan Šević (Serbian: Јован Шевић , Russian: Иван Егорович Шевич ; died  1764 ) was an 18th-century military officer of Serb origin.

candidates.title: Jovan Šević
candidates.text: He reached the rank of lieutenant colonel in the Serb militia forces in the Pomorišje region, then in the Military Frontier of the Habsburg Monarchy.

candidates.title: Jovan Šević
candidates.text: When it became obvious that privileges granted to Serb militiamen would be reduced or completely revoked after Pomorišje and Potisje lost their frontier status, Šević left Habsburg military service in 1750 and moved to Russia.

candidates.title: Jovan Šević
candidates.text: At the end of 1752, he led the second wave of colonists who migrated from Pomorišje, Potisje and Slavonia to the Russian Empire (modern-day Ukraine) where they settled the newly established administrative region of Slavo-Serbia at the beginning of 1753.

candidates.title: Jovan Šević
candidates.text: To enable him to recruit more of his fellow officers, Šević was promoted to the rank of General by the Russian Empress, Elizabeth.

candidates.title: Jovan Šević
candidates.text: He commanded a Serb Hussar Regiment consisting of the colonists he brought to Russia.

candidates.title: Jovan Šević
candidates.text: After Šević's death, Slavo-Serbia was disestablished, and many of his descendants became notable military officers in the Russian Imperial Army.

candidates.title: Jovan Šević
candidates.text: Over time, all the Serb colonists became assimilated.

candidates.title: Serb uprising of 1737–39

candidates.title: Serb uprising of 1737–39

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The history of paleontology in the United States refers to the developments and discoveries regarding fossils found within or by people from the United States of America.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: Local paleontology began informally with Native Americans, who have been familiar with fossils for thousands of years.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: They both told myths about them and applied them to practical purposes.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: African slaves also contributed their knowledge; the first reasonably accurate recorded identification of vertebrate fossils in the new world was made by slaves on a South Carolina plantation who recognized the elephant affinities of mammoth molars uncovered there in 1725.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: The first major fossil discovery to attract the attention of formally trained scientists were the Ice Age fossils of Kentucky's Big Bone Lick.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: These fossils were studied by eminent intellectuals like France's George Cuvier and local statesmen and frontiersman like Daniel Boone, Benjamin Franklin, William Henry Harrison, Thomas Jefferson, and George Washington.

candidates.title: History of paleontology in the United States
candidates.text: By the end of the 18th century possible dinosaur fossils had already been found.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Big Bone Lick State Park is located at Big Bone in Boone County, Kentucky.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The name of the park comes from the Pleistocene megafauna fossils found there.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Mammoths are believed to have been drawn to this location by a salt lick deposited around sulphur springs.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: Other animals including forms of bison, caribou, deer, elk, horse, mastodon, moose, musk ox, peccary, sloth, and possibly tapir also grazed the vegetation and salty earth around the springs that the animals relied on for their diet.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: The area near the springs was very soft and marshy causing many animals to become stuck with no way to escape.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: It bills itself as "the birthplace of American paleontology", a term which dates from the 1807 expedition by William Clark undertaken at the direction of President Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In Nicholas Cresswell's journal, dated 1774 to 1777, he records a visit in 1775 to what was then called "Elephant Bone Lick."

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: In this account, Cresswell describes finding several bones of "prodigious size", as well as tusk fragments, and teeth—one weighing approximately 10 pounds.

candidates.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
candidates.text: While he assumed the bones were from ancient elephants, the local native traditions claimed the bones to be those of white buffaloes that had been poisoned by the salty water.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Paleontology in Kentucky refers to paleontological research occurring within or conducted by people from the U.S. state of Kentucky.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Kentucky's abundance of exposed sedimentary rock makes it an ideal source of fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The oldest exposed rocks in Kentucky are of Ordovician age.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: The geologic column of Kentucky also contains rocks deposited during the ensuing periods until the end of the Pennsylvanian.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During this span of time the state was first home to a warm shallow sea home to an abundance and variety of brachiopods, cephalopods, crinoids, and trilobites.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: During the Devonian, a large reef system formed at what is now the Falls of the Ohio.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Swamps covered Kentucky during the ensuing Carboniferous period.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Then a gap spans from the start of the Permian to the Pleistocene, although the gap is interrupted by minor deposits of Cretaceous and Eocene rocks.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: These deposits mainly preserve plant fossils.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Ice Age Kentucky was home to short-faced bear, bison, elk, lions, mammoths, mastodons, and giant ground sloths.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Local Native Americans interpreted fossils of this age at Big Bone Lick as belonging to ancient monsters killed by benevolent mystical little people.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: This same fossil deposit would attract attention from major American figures like George Washington, Daniel Boone, and, especially, Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Amateur fossil collectors should be aware that they need permission from landowners to prospect legally on private property.

candidates.title: Paleontology in Kentucky
candidates.text: Brachiopods are the Kentucky state fossil.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: Big Bone is an unincorporated community in southern Boone County, Kentucky, United States.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: It is bounded on the west by the Ohio River, and Rabbit Hash, on the south by Big Bone Creek, which empties into the river at Big Bone Landing.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: The northern extent is along Hathaway Road, and the eastern portion extends not further than U.S. 42, and is approached from that direction by Beaver Road (Route 338) coming from either Richwood or Walton.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: Big Bone took its name from a nearby prehistoric mineral lick of the same name.

candidates.title: Big Bone, Kentucky
candidates.text: Geographical features of interest include the now disappeared Big Bone Island and the Palisades of Big Bone Creek.

candidates.title: Thomas Jefferson
candidates.text: Thomas Jefferson (April 13 [O.S. April 2] 1743 – July 4, 1826) was an American Founding Father who was the principal author of the Declaration of Independence and later served as the third President of the United States from 1801 to 1809.

candidates.title: Thomas Jefferson
candidates.text: Previously, he was elected the second Vice President of the United States, serving under John Adams from 1797 to 1801.

candidates.title: Thomas Jefferson
candidates.text: A proponent of democracy, republicanism, and individual rights motivating American colonists to break from Great Britain and form a new nation, he produced formative documents and decisions at both the state and national level.

candidates.title: Thomas Jefferson
candidates.text: He was a land owner and farmer.

candidates.title: Jefferson County, Oklahoma
candidates.text: Its county seat is Waurika.

candidates.title: Jefferson County, Oklahoma
candidates.text: The county was created at statehood and named in honor of President Thomas Jefferson.

candidates.title: Charles Carroll of Annapolis
candidates.text: Charles Carroll II (1702–1782) known as Charles Carroll of Annapolis to distinguish him from his similarly named relatives, was a wealthy Maryland planter and lawyer.

candidates.title: Charles Carroll of Annapolis
candidates.text: His father was Charles Carroll the Settler, (I – the first), (1661–1720), an immigrant to Maryland who had arrived in the colony in 1689 with a commission as Provincial Attorney General, and had accumulated a vast fortune, emerging as Maryland's wealthiest citizen.

candidates.title: Charles Carroll of Annapolis
candidates.text: Charles Carroll of Annapolis inherited and extended his father's fortune but, as a Roman Catholic, was barred from participation in Maryland politics.

candidates.title: Charles Carroll of Annapolis
candidates.text: It would fall to his son, Charles Carroll of Carrollton, (III), (1737–1832), one of the signers (and the longest-lived) of the Declaration of Independence, to see religious toleration restored to Maryland and many political and scientific/technological advances in the newly independent state.

candidates.title: Bharat Ratna
candidates.text: The Bharat Ratna (] ; "Jewel of India") is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India.

candidates.title: Bharat Ratna
candidates.text: Instituted in 1954, the award is conferred "in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order", without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex.

candidates.title: Bharat Ratna
candidates.text: The award was originally limited to achievements in the arts, literature, science, and public services, but the government expanded the criteria to include "any field of human endeavour" in December 2011.

candidates.title: Bharat Ratna
candidates.text: The recommendations for the Bharat Ratna are made by the Prime Minister to the President, with a maximum of three nominees being awarded per year.

candidates.title: Bharat Ratna
candidates.text: Recipients receive a "Sanad" (certificate) signed by the President and a peepal-leaf–shaped medallion; there is no monetary grant associated with the award.

candidates.title: Bharat Ratna
candidates.text: Bharat Ratna recipients rank seventh in the Indian order of precedence.

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: The Padma Bhushan is the third highest civilian honour of the Republic of India, preceded by the Padma Vibhushan and followed by the Padma Shri.

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: Presented by the Government of India since 1954 for "distinguished service of a high order", without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex, the award consists of a certificate and a medallion and the recipient's name is registered in "The Gazette of India".

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: When instituted, the Padma Bhushan was classified as "Dusra Warg", a class-two award under the three-tier Padma Vibhushan awards, which were preceded by the Bharat Ratna in hierarchy.

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: On 15January 1955, the Padma Vibhushan was reclassified into three different awards as the Padma Vibhushan, the highest of the three, followed by the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Shri.

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: The Padma Bhushan, along with other personal civilian honours, was briefly suspended twice since its inception; for the first time in July 1977 and the suspension was annulled on 25 January 1980 by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: The civilian awards were suspended again in mid-1992 for it being "titles" per an interpretation of of the Constitution of India.

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: On 25 August 1992, the Madhya Pradesh High Court issued a notice temporarily suspending all civilian awards.

candidates.title: List of Padma Bhushan award recipients (2010–19)
candidates.text: On 15 December 1995, the Special Division Bench restored the awards and delivered a judgment that the "Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not titles under Article 18 of the Constitution of India".

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The hill rises about 250 feet above the level of the plateau, which itself constitutes the summit of the Mahadev range at this point.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The cone with the walls on it is seen from a great distance and appears very small indeed.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: But on near approach it is seen to be but the inner citadel of a place of considerable size and strength for the times in which it was built.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: On the south-west the outer wall or enceinte is entered by a rude gateway of a single pointed arch about eight feet high and five feet broad.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: As usual there is a curtain of solid masonry inside.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The gate lies about 150 yards east of the edge of the plateau, which there terminates in an almost unbroken vertical precipice of several hundred feet in height and receding in a north-easterly direction.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: No wall was built along about three hundred yards of this part which is absolutely unscalable, but for the rest of the way the walling is continued along the edge of the cliff in a north-east direction for about another three hundred yards.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: Here it turns still following the cliff to the south-east for another seven hundred yards, and then gradually rounds to the westward covering four hundred and fifty yards more till it meets the gateway.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: But for the break of the inaccessible precipice this outer wall would form a nearly equilateral triangle with the corners rounded off, the side being of some six hundred and fifty yards.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: Facing nearly north, about fifty yards from the north-east angle, is a gateway with a couple of curtains in solid masonry.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: This entrance is cut in the sides of the cliff about twenty feet below the top which is reached by some dozen steps.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: It consisted as usual of a pointed arch, the top fallen in, about ten feet high by five broad.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: It leads out to the path down to Girvi, a village in the plains below and it probably formed the communication with Phaltan.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: This road winds down the face of the range for some five hundred feet till it hits the shoulder of a spur which it then follows to the base.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The walling on the south side, from the edge of the cliff to some hundred yards east of the southern gate, is not more than a couple of feet in thickness and consists of all-fitting stones unmortared.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The rest is massive and well mortared and still fairly preserved.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The average height is from seven to ten feet.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: In the south-east angle is a rude temple of Bhairavnath and a few houses with the remains of Man y more.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: On the right side of the southern gate is a well preserved stone pond about thirty yards square with steps leading down to it.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: Next to and on the north of Bhairavnath's temple is another pond.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The way up to the fort proper or upper and lower citadels is from the north side.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The path up the hill side, which is steep but with grass and soil left in Man y places, is almost destroyed.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: About 150 feet up is the outer citadel built on a sort of shoulder of the hill and facing almost due west.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: It contains two massive bastions of excellent masonry looking north-west and south-west so that guns planted on them could comMan d respectively the north and south gateways.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: This citadel was connected with the main wall by a cross wall running across the whole breadth of the fort from east to west.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: Its entrance lies close below that to the upper citadel.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: A masonry curtain projects so as to hide the arch itself, which is not more than seven feet high by three broad, and has to be entered from due east.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: On the south side the walls are carried right up to the scarp of the upper citadel and are some ten feet high, so that to take the lower citadel in rear or flank must have been difficult.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The upper citadel is above a vertical scarp some thirty feet high.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The entrance to it lies some thirty feet above that to the lower citadel, and is cut in the rock about eight feet wide.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: There is a gateway of a pointed arch with the top fallen in and twenty odd steps leading up to it and ten more cut out of the rock, and winding up past the inside curtain on to the top.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The walls of this upper citadel are still in tolerable preservation.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: They were originally about ten feet high and built of fair masonry.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: There is a large turret on the south-west corner, evidently meant to comMan d the southern gate.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: About ten yards to the east of this turret is a new looking building which was the headquarters or sadar.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: Immediately east of this and below it is a great pit about thirty feet square and equally deep roughly cut in the rock and said by the people to be a dungeon.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: Next to it on the south is a small pond evenly cut and lined with mortar used for storing water.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: There are some remains of sepoys' houses, and, near the turret, a small stone wheel said to belong to a gun.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The outer walls east of the gates have bastions at every turn of the cliffs, and the masonry here is particularly strong and well preserved.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: It would appear that attacks were dreaded chiefly from the plain below.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The assailants could either come up the spur towards the north entrance or they might attempt the spurs on the other side of the eastern ravine and attack the southern gateway.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: Hence apparently the reason for strengthening the walls of the enceinte on this side.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: After passing the southern gateway the assailants would be commanded Maan, Maharashtra from the lower citadel.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: They Would then be encountered by the cross wall.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: If that obstacle was overcome the besieged would run round the east side and into the two citadels.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The appearance from the fort of the plain in the north is most formidable.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The Panvan plateau completely commands Maan, Maharashtra and almost overhangs it.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The fort is believed to have been built by Shivaji to resist the Moghals whose attacks he must have dreaded from the plain below.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The Karkhanis or Superintendent of the fort was a Prabhu.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: The fort garrison consisted of 200 Ramoshis, Mahars, and other hereditary Gadkaris besides sepoys.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: It was surrendered in 1818 to Vitthal Pant Phadnis of the Raja of Satara left in charge of the town.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: He detached 200 men to take possession, being part of a force then raised to protect the town from the enterprizes of Bajirav's garrisons then in the neighbourhood.

candidates.title: Varugad
candidates.text: [Elphinstone in Pendhari and Maratha War Papers, 245.]

candidates.title: Cardiff Castle
candidates.text: Cardiff Castle (Welsh: "Castell Caerdydd" ) is a medieval castle and Victorian Gothic revival mansion located in the city centre of Cardiff, Wales.

candidates.title: Cardiff Castle
candidates.text: The original motte and bailey castle was built in the late 11th century by Norman invaders on top of a 3rd-century Roman fort.

candidates.title: Cardiff Castle
candidates.text: The castle was commissioned either by William the Conqueror or by Robert Fitzhamon, and formed the heart of the medieval town of Cardiff and the Marcher Lord territory of Glamorgan.

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: Dance music is music composed specifically to facilitate or accompany dancing.

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: It can be either a whole musical piece or part of a larger musical arrangement.

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: In terms of performance, the major categories are live dance music and recorded dance music.

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: While there exist attestations of the combination of dance and music in ancient times (for example Ancient Greek vases sometimes show dancers accompanied by musicians), the earliest Western dance music that we can still reproduce with a degree of certainty are the surviving medieval dances.

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: In the Baroque period, the major dance styles were noble court dances (see Baroque dance).

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: In the classical music era, the minuet was frequently used as a third movement, although in this context it would not accompany any dancing.

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: The waltz also arose later in the classical era.

candidates.title: Dance music
candidates.text: Both remained part of the romantic music period, which also saw the rise of various other nationalistic dance forms like the barcarolle, mazurka, ecossaise, ballade and polonaise.

candidates.title: Persian dance
candidates.text: Persian dance or Iranian dance (Persian:رقص ایرانی) refers to the dance styles indigenous to Iran.

candidates.title: Persian dance
candidates.text: Genres of dance in Iran vary depending on the area, culture, and language of the local people, and can range from sophisticated reconstructions of refined court dances to energetic folk dances.

candidates.title: Persian dance
candidates.text: The population of Iran includes many ethnicities, such as Kurds, Azerbaijanis, Turkmen, Jews, Armenian, Georgian peoples, in addition to numerous Iranian tribal groups which can be found within the borders of modern-day Iran.

candidates.title: Persian dance
candidates.text: Each group, region, and historical epoch has specific dance styles associated with it.

candidates.title: Persian dance
candidates.text: Raghs (also spelled as Raqs) is the Arabic word for dance, and is almost exclusively the word used for dance in Persian, as the Persian word for dance, paykubi, is no longer in common usage.

candidates.title: Persian dance
candidates.text: It's also the word in Azerbaijani for dance ("Reqs").

candidates.title: Persian dance
candidates.text: The Kurdish word for dance is Halperke, and the Lurs from Lorestan use the word Bākhten (or Bāzee) for dance.

candidates.title: Hip-hop dance
candidates.text: Hip-hop dance refers to street dance styles primarily performed to hip-hop music or that have evolved as part of hip-hop culture.

candidates.title: Hip-hop dance
candidates.text: It includes a wide range of styles primarily breaking which was created in the 1970s and made popular by dance crews in the United States.

candidates.title: Hip-hop dance
candidates.text: The television show "Soul Train" and the 1980s films "Breakin'", "Beat Street", and "Wild Style" showcased these crews and dance styles in their early stages; therefore, giving hip-hop mainstream exposure.

candidates.title: Hip-hop dance
candidates.text: The dance industry responded with a commercial, studio-based version of hip-hop—sometimes called "new style"—and a hip-hop influenced style of jazz dance called "jazz-funk".

candidates.title: Hip-hop dance
candidates.text: Classically trained dancers developed these studio styles in order to choreograph from the hip-hop dances that were performed on the street.

candidates.title: Hip-hop dance
candidates.text: Because of this development, hip-hop dance is practiced in both dance studios and outdoor spaces.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: Cuban culture encompasses a wide range of dance forms.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: The island's indigenous people performed rituals known as areíto, which included dancing, although little information is known about such ceremonies.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: After the colonization of Cuba by the Spanish Kingdom, European dance forms were introduced such as the French contredanse, which gave rise to the Cuban contradanza.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: Contradanza itself spawned a series of ballroom dances between the 19th and 20th centuries, including the danzón, mambo and cha-cha-cha.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: Rural dances of European origin, such as the zapateo and styles associated with punto guajiro also became established by the 19th century, and in the 20th century son became very popular.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: In addition, numerous dance traditions were brought by black slaves from West Africa and the Congo basin, giving rise to religious dances such as Santería, yuka and abakuá, as well as secular forms such as rumba.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: Many of these dance elements from European dance and religious dances were fused together to form the basis of la técnica cubana.

candidates.title: Dance in Cuba
candidates.text: Cuban music also contributed to the emergence of Latin dance styles in the United States, namely rhumba (ballroom rumba) and salsa.

candidates.text: This is the main list of dances.

candidates.title: List of dances
candidates.text: It is a non-categorized, index list of specific dances.

candidates.title: List of dances
candidates.text: There may also be listed dances which could either be considered specific dances or a family of related dances, depending on your perspective.

candidates.title: List of dances
candidates.text: For example, ballet, ballroom dance and folk dance can be single dance styles or families of related dances.

candidates.title: List of dances
candidates.text: The purpose of the page is to have as complete an index as possible.

candidates.text: Baroque dance is dance of the Baroque era (roughly 1600-1750), closely linked with Baroque music, theatre and opera.

candidates.title: Jianianhualong
candidates.text: Despite aerodynamic differences from the flight feathers of modern birds, the feathers comprising the tail vane of "Jianianhualong" would still have likely functioned in drag reduction whilst the animal was moving.

candidates.title: Jianianhualong

candidates.text: Whole life insurance, or whole of life assurance (in the Commonwealth of Nations), sometimes called "straight life" or "ordinary life," is a life insurance policy which is guaranteed to remain in force for the insured's entire lifetime, provided required premiums are paid, or to the maturity date.

candidates.title: Birthday effect
candidates.text: The birthday effect (sometimes called the birthday blues, especially when referring specifically to suicide) is a statistical phenomenon where an individual's likelihood of death appears to increase on or close to their birthday.

candidates.title: Birthday effect
candidates.text: The birthday effect has been seen in studies of general populations in England and Wales, Switzerland, Ukraine, and the United States, as well as in smaller populations such as Major League Baseball players.

candidates.title: Birthday effect
candidates.text: Studies do not consistently show this effect; some studies find that men's and women's mortality rates diverge in the run-up to the birthday, while others find no significant gender effect.

candidates.title: Birthday effect
candidates.text: Suggested mechanisms for the effect include alcohol consumption, psychological stress relating to the birthday, increased suicide risk, terminally ill patients attempting to hold on until their birthday, an increased mortality salience, or a physiological cycle that causes the body to weaken annually.

candidates.title: Birthday effect
candidates.text: It has also been suggested that it may be a statistical artifact, perhaps as a result of anomalies in reporting, but the birthday effect has also been seen in studies that control for known reporting anomalies.

candidates.title: Give Me a Home Among the Gumtrees
candidates.text: Give Me a Home Among the Gumtrees (or Home Among the Gumtrees) is a popular Australian song written in 1974 by Wally Johnson and Bob Brown (aka Captain Rock).

candidates.title: Give Me a Home Among the Gumtrees
candidates.text: It was originally performed as a satirical number in Johnson and Brown's comedy act at the Flying Trapeze Cafe in Fitzroy, Melbourne and was first recorded in 1975 on the Captain Rock album "Buried Treasure" on Mushroom Records.

candidates.title: God Save the Queen
candidates.text: "God Save the Queen" (alternatively "God Save the King", depending on the gender of the reigning monarch) is the national or royal anthem in a number of Commonwealth realms, their territories, and the British Crown Dependencies.

candidates.title: God Save the Queen
candidates.text: The author of the tune is unknown and it may originate in plainchant, but a 1619 attribution to John Bull is sometimes made.

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: "E Ola Ke Aliʻ i Ke Akua", translated as "God Save the King", was one of Hawaii's four national anthems.

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: It was composed in 1860 by Prince William Charles Lunalilo, who later became King Lunalilo.

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: Prior to 1860, the Kingdom of Hawaii lacked its own national anthem and had used the British royal anthem "God Save The King".

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: A contest was sponsored in 1860 by Kamehameha IV, who wanted a song with Hawaiian lyrics set to the tune of the British anthem.

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: The winning entry was written by the 25-year-old Lunalilo and was reputed to have been written in 20 minutes.

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: Lunalilo was awarded 10 dollars, which later donated to the Queen's Hospital.

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: His composition became Hawaii's first national anthem.

candidates.title: E Ola Ke Alii Ke Akua
candidates.text: It remained Hawaii's national anthem until 1866, when it was replaced by Queen Liliʻ uokalani's composition "He Mele Lahui Hawaii".

candidates.title: Long live our noble Duke
candidates.text: "Long live our noble Duke" is an alteration traditionally made within the historic county boundaries of Lancashire to the anthem 'God Save the Queen'.

candidates.title: Long live our noble Duke
candidates.text: The anthem still uses the same lyrics and instrumental tune, but the second line "Long live our noble Queen" is changed to "Long live our noble Duke" out of respect to the reigning monarch in their capacity as the Duke of Lancaster.

candidates.title: Long live our noble Duke
candidates.text: The title is always held by the monarch as head of the royal Duchy of Lancaster, historically Lancaster being the county town of Lancashire.

candidates.title: Long live our noble Duke
candidates.text: No matter if the sovereign is male or female, they always retain the style of Duke, therefore the variant second line never changes even if 'God save the Queen' changes to 'God Save the King' and vice versa.

candidates.title: Proposals for a national anthem for England
candidates.text: The national anthem of England is usually taken to be the same as that of the United Kingdom as a whole—"God Save the Queen", but some feel that England should have its own distinct anthem, and there are a number of songs which may fulfil a similar role.

candidates.title: Proposals for a national anthem for England

candidates.title: Proposals for a national anthem for England
candidates.text: There have been discussions on the subject in the UK Parliament.

candidates.title: Proposals for a national anthem for England

candidates.title: Extended order
candidates.text: Extended order is an economics and sociology concept introduced by Friedrich Hayek in his book "The Fatal Conceit".

candidates.title: Extended order

candidates.title: Extended order
candidates.text: The extended order is at the heart of Hayek's thesis, in "The Fatal Conceit", where he argues that "our civilization depends, not only for its origin but also for its preservation, on what can be precisely described only as the extended order of human cooperation, an order more commonly, if somewhat misleading, known as capitalism.”

candidates.title: Sraffa–Hayek debate

candidates.title: Sraffa–Hayek debate

candidates.title: Arrested Development (TV series)
candidates.text: Ron Howard serves as both an executive producer and the series' uncredited narrator.

candidates.title: Arrested Development (TV series)
candidates.text: Set in Newport Beach, California, "Arrested Development" was filmed primarily in Culver City and Marina del Rey.

candidates.title: Culver CityBus
candidates.text: Culver CityBus is a public transport agency operating in Culver City, California, currently serving Culver City, the unincorporated community of Marina del Rey, and the adjacent Los Angeles neighborhoods.

candidates.title: Culver CityBus
candidates.text: Its regular fleet is painted bright green and its rapid fleet primarily a chrome gray, distinguishing it from Santa Monica's Big Blue Bus, orange-colored Metro Local buses, and red-colored Metro Rapid buses, whose coverage areas overlap on Los Angeles's Westside.

candidates.title: Ballona Creek
candidates.text: Ballona Creek is an 8.8 mi waterway in southwestern Los Angeles County, California, whose watershed drains the Los Angeles basin, from the Santa Monica Mountains on the north, the Harbor Freeway (I-110) on the east, and the Baldwin Hills on the south.

candidates.title: Ballona Creek
candidates.text: It heads in the historical Rancho Las Cienegas and flows through Culver City and the Del Rey district before emptying into Santa Monica Bay between Marina del Rey and the Playa del Rey district.

candidates.title: Ballona Wetlands
candidates.text: The Ballona Wetlands are located in Southern California, United States south of Marina del Rey and east of Playa del Rey.

candidates.title: Ballona Wetlands
candidates.text: The wetlands once included the areas now taken up by Marina del Rey, Venice, and Playa Vista, extending north to about present-day Washington Blvd. in Venice.

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: American singer and occasional actress Lana Del Rey has appeared in three films as an actress, eighteen television shows, and three commercials, along with offering her talents to five films as singer.

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: Del Rey's first appearance was in the independent film "Poolside" (2010), which features Del Rey playing Lisa, a rich girl who spends her days smoking cigarettes by the pool.

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: She received top billing for the project.

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: Del Rey's next appearance was in a less-than-one-minute long short art film titled "Lana Del Rey" which was produced by Interview magazine and features noir-ish style and cinematic themes.

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: Del Rey's breakout appearance was in an Anthony Mandler directed film, which Del Rey wrote, titled "Tropico" (2013).

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: The film features Del Rey as a fictionalized version of Eve while also playing the Virgin Mary.

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: "Tropico" received positive reviews and was Del Rey's second film that gave her top billing.

candidates.title: Lana Del Rey videography
candidates.text: Along with appearing in a handful of short films, Del Rey has appeared in 18 television shows and specials as herself along with appearing in campaign commercials for companies including Keds and H&M.

candidates.title: Judy Greer
candidates.text: Judith Therese Evans (born July 20, 1975), known as Judy Greer, is an American actress, model and author, known for several television and film roles.

candidates.title: Judy Greer
candidates.text: On television, her best known roles include Kitty Sanchez on "Arrested Development", Ingrid Nelson/Fatty Magoo on "It's Always Sunny In Philadelphia", Trixie on "Californication", and Cheryl Tunt on the animated comedy series "Archer".

candidates.title: Judy Greer
candidates.text: In film, Greer is known for several supporting roles in romantic comedies, with appearances in "What Women Want" (2000), "The Wedding Planner" (2001), "13 Going on 30" (2004), "27 Dresses" (2008) and "Love & Other Drugs" (2010).

candidates.title: Judy Greer
candidates.text: Her other film appearances include roles in "The Descendants" (2011), "Carrie" (2013) and "Jurassic World" (2015).

candidates.title: Visioneers
candidates.text: Visioneers is a 2008 satirical dark comedy directed by Jared Drake and written by Brandon Drake.

candidates.title: Visioneers
candidates.text: The film stars comedian Zach Galifianakis and actress Judy Greer.

candidates.title: Visioneers
candidates.text: The film premiered on June 12, 2008.

candidates.title: Visioneers
candidates.text: The film was shot in Snoqualmie, Washington and surrounding areas.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar (film)
candidates.text: The Bell Jar is a 1979 film based on Sylvia Plath's 1963 book "The Bell Jar".

candidates.title: The Bell Jar (film)
candidates.text: It was directed by Larry Peerce, and stars Marilyn Hassett and Julie Harris.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar (film)
candidates.text: The story follows a young woman's summer in New York City working for a women's magazine, her return home to New England, and her subsequent psychological breakdown within the context of the difficulties of the 1950s—ranging from the Rosenbergs' execution, to the disturbing aspects of pop culture, to the distraction of predatory college boys.

candidates.title: Samuel Eliot Morison
candidates.text: Samuel Eliot Morison, (July 9, 1887 – May 15, 1976) was an American historian noted for his works of maritime history and American history that were both authoritative and popular.

candidates.title: Samuel Eliot Morison
candidates.text: He received his Ph.D. from Harvard University in 1912, and taught history at the university for 40 years.

candidates.title: Samuel Eliot Morison
candidates.text: He won Pulitzer Prizes for "Admiral of the Ocean Sea" (1942), a biography of Christopher Columbus, and "John Paul Jones: A Sailor's Biography" (1959).

candidates.title: Samuel Eliot Morison
candidates.text: In 1942, he was commissioned to write a history of United States naval operations in World War II, which was published in 15 volumes between 1947 and 1962.

candidates.title: Samuel Eliot Morison
candidates.text: Morison wrote the popular "Oxford History of the American People" (1965), and co-authored the classic textbook "The Growth of the American Republic" (1930) with Henry Steele Commager.

candidates.title: Samuel Eliot Morison
candidates.text: Over the course of his distinguished career, Morison received eleven honorary doctoral degrees, and garnered numerous literary prizes, military honors, and national awards from both foreign countries and the United States, including two Pulitzer Prizes, two Bancroft Prizes, the Balzan Prize, the Legion of Merit, and the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

candidates.title: Bell jar
candidates.text: A bell jar is a glass jar, similar in shape to a bell, and can be manufactured from a variety of materials (ranging from glass to different types of metals).

candidates.title: Bell jar
candidates.text: Bell jars are often used in laboratories to form and contain a vacuum; they may also serve as display cases or transparent dust covers.

candidates.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
candidates.text: The 2011 Pulitzer Prizes were announced on Monday, April 18, 2011.

candidates.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
candidates.text: "The Los Angeles Times" won two prizes, including the highest honor for Public Service.

candidates.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
candidates.text: "The New York Times" also won two awards.

candidates.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
candidates.text: No prize was handed out in the Breaking News category.

candidates.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
candidates.text: "The Wall Street Journal" won an award for the first time since 2007.

candidates.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
candidates.text: Jennifer Egan's "A Visit From the Goon Squad" picked up the Fiction prize after already winning the 2010 National Book Critics Circle Award.

candidates.title: 2011 Pulitzer Prize
candidates.text: Photographer Carol Guzy of "The Washington Post" became the first journalist to win four Pulitzer Prizes.

candidates.title: Pulitzer Prize for Photography
candidates.text: The Pulitzer Prize for Photography was one of the American Pulitzer Prizes annually awarded for journalism.

candidates.title: Pulitzer Prize for Photography
candidates.text: It was inaugurated in 1942 and replaced by two photojournalism prizes in 1968: the Pulitzer Prize for Feature Photography and "Pulitzer Prize for Spot News Photography".

candidates.title: Pulitzer Prize for Photography
candidates.text: The latter was renamed for Pulitzer Prize for Breaking News Photography in 2000.

candidates.title: Sylvia Plath
candidates.text: Sylvia Plath ( ; October 27, 1932 – February 11, 1963) was an American poet, novelist, and short story writer.

candidates.title: Sylvia Plath
candidates.text: Born in Boston, she studied at Smith College and Newnham College at the University of Cambridge before receiving acclaim as a poet and writer.

candidates.title: Sylvia Plath
candidates.text: She married fellow poet Ted Hughes in 1956, and they lived together in the United States and then in England.

candidates.title: Sylvia Plath
candidates.text: They had two children, Frieda and Nicholas, before separating in 1962.

candidates.title: Sylvia Plath
candidates.text: Plath was clinically depressed for most of her adult life, and was treated multiple times with electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).

candidates.title: Sylvia Plath
candidates.text: She committed suicide in 1963.

candidates.title: Michael Cunningham
candidates.text: Michael Cunningham (born November 6, 1952) is a U.S. novelist and screenwriter.

candidates.title: Michael Cunningham
candidates.text: He is best known for his 1998 novel "The Hours", which won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and the PEN/Faulkner Award in 1999.

candidates.title: Michael Cunningham
candidates.text: Cunningham is a senior lecturer of creative writing at Yale University.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar
candidates.text: The Bell Jar is the only novel written by the American writer and poet Sylvia Plath.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar
candidates.text: Originally published under the pseudonym "Victoria Lucas" in 1963, the novel is semi-autobiographical, with the names of places and people changed.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar
candidates.text: The book is often regarded as a "roman à clef" since the protagonist's descent into mental illness parallels Plath's own experiences with what may have been clinical depression.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar
candidates.text: Plath died by suicide a month after its first UK publication.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar
candidates.text: The novel was published under Plath's name for the first time in 1967 and was not published in the United States until 1971, in accordance with the wishes of both Plath's husband, Ted Hughes, and her mother.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar
candidates.text: The novel has been translated into nearly a dozen languages.

candidates.title: The Bell Jar
candidates.text: The novel, though dark, is often read in high school English classes.

candidates.title: Mary Abigail Fillmore
candidates.text: Mary Abigail "Abbie" Powers Fillmore (March 27, 1832, Buffalo, New York – July 26, 1854, East Aurora, New York) was the daughter of President Millard Fillmore and Abigail Powers.

candidates.title: Mary Abigail Fillmore
candidates.text: During her father's presidency from 1850 to 1853 she often served as White House hostess, in part due to her mother's illness.

candidates.title: Texans for Public Justice
candidates.text: Texans for Public Justice (TPJ) is an Austin-based non-profit group founded in 1997 to take on political corruption and corporate abuses in Texas, United States.

candidates.title: Texans for Public Justice
candidates.text: Their early focus was on tracking campaign contributions in Texas and elsewhere, including contributions to George W. Bush's campaign in the 2000 and 2004 US presidential elections.

candidates.title: Texans for Public Justice
candidates.text: The group lodged the original complainant that led to the now overturned conviction of former US Representative Tom Delay, as well as current Texas Governor Rick Perry's widely criticized August 2014 felony indictment.

candidates.title: James Smith Bush
candidates.text: Rev. James Smith Bush (June 15, 1825 – November 11, 1889) was an American attorney, Episcopal priest, religious writer, and an ancestor of the Bush political family.

candidates.title: James Smith Bush
candidates.text: He was the father of business magnate Samuel Prescott Bush, grandfather of former US Senator Prescott Bush, great-grandfather of former US President George H. W. Bush and great-great-grandfather of former US President George W. Bush.

candidates.title: Matson Trial
candidates.text: The Matson Trial (1847), officially Matson v. Ashmore et al. for the use of Bryant, was a freedom suit by former slave Anthony Bryant on behalf of his family in Coles County, Illinois.

candidates.title: Matson Trial
candidates.text: It is noted for the unusual circumstance where Abraham Lincoln, the future emancipator of slaves, defended a slave-owner against a slave.

candidates.title: Matson Trial
candidates.text: The case pitted Lincoln and former Illinois Attorney General Usher F. Linder against former US Representative Orlando B. Ficklin.

candidates.title: Matson Trial
candidates.text: Ficklin's case proved successful, and Bryant's family was emancipated based on free soil doctrine.

candidates.title: Citizens' Climate Lobby
candidates.text: Citizens' Climate Lobby (CCL) is an international grassroots environmental group that trains and supports volunteers to build relationships with their elected representatives in order to influence climate policy.

candidates.title: Citizens' Climate Lobby
candidates.text: The CCL is a registered 501(c)(4) with approximately $300 thousand in revenue in the United States in 2015.

candidates.title: Citizens' Climate Lobby
candidates.text: Operating since 2007, the goal of CCL is to build political support across party lines to put a price on carbon, specifically a revenue neutral carbon fee and dividend (CF&D) at the national level.

candidates.title: Citizens' Climate Lobby
candidates.text: CCL is supported by notable climate scientists James Hansen, Katharine Hayhoe, and Daniel Kammen.

candidates.title: Citizens' Climate Lobby
candidates.text: CCL's advisory board also includes former Secretary of State George P. Shultz, former US Representative Bob Inglis, actor Don Cheadle, and RESULTS founder Sam Daley-Harris.

candidates.title: Nathaniel Fillmore
candidates.text: Nathaniel Fillmore Jr. (April 19, 1771 – March 28, 1863) was an American farmer, and the father of Millard Fillmore, the 13th President of the United States.

candidates.title: Millard Fillmore
candidates.text: Millard Fillmore (January 7, 1800March 8, 1874) was the 13th President of the United States (1850–53), the last to be a member of the Whig Party while in the White House.

candidates.title: Millard Fillmore
candidates.text: A former U.S. Representative from New York, Fillmore was elected the nation's 12th Vice President in 1848, and was elevated to the presidency by the death of Zachary Taylor.

candidates.title: Millard Fillmore
candidates.text: He was instrumental in getting the Compromise of 1850 passed, a bargain that led to a brief truce in the battle over slavery.

candidates.title: Millard Fillmore
candidates.text: He failed to win the Whig nomination for president in 1852; he gained the endorsement of the nativist Know Nothing Party four years later, and finished third in that election.
